questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: The following carbocation is stabilized by the interaction of the empty $p$ orbital with
questions.solution:
The given carbocation has a positively charged carbon atom that is $sp^2$ hybridized, possessing an empty unhybridized p-orbital.

This empty p-orbital is stabilized by hyperconjugation, where the filled C-H $\sigma$ bonding orbitals of the adjacent methyl group overlap with the empty p-orbital to donate electron density.

Additionally, it is stabilized by resonance, where the filled $\pi$ bonding orbitals of the adjacent benzene ring overlap with the empty p-orbital to delocalize $\pi$ electrons.

Thus, the stabilization occurs through the interaction of the empty p-orbital with filled $\sigma$ and filled $\pi$ orbitals.

Answer: filled $\sigma$ and filled $\pi$ orbitals

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: The pair of molecules that are metamers among the following is :
questions.solution:
Metamerism is a type of structural isomerism where isomers have the same molecular formula but differ in the nature of the alkyl groups attached to the same polyvalent functional group (such as $-\text{O}-$, $-\text{S}-$, $-\text{NH}-$, $-\text{CO}-$).

In option (1), $\text{CH}_3\text{CH}_2\text{CH}_2\text{OH}$ and $\text{CH}_3-\text{CH(OH)}-\text{CH}_3$ are position isomers because the position of the $-\text{OH}$ group differs.

In option (2), $\text{CH}_3\text{CH}_2\text{CH}_2\text{CH}_2\text{CH}_3$ and $(\text{CH}_3)_2\text{CHCH}_2\text{CH}_3$ are chain isomers because the carbon skeleton differs.

In option (3), $\text{H}_3\text{C}-\text{CO}-\text{CH}_3$ and $\text{H}_3\text{C}-\text{CH}_2-\text{CHO}$ are functional isomers because they have different functional groups (ketone and aldehyde).

In option (4), $\text{CH}_3\text{OCH}_2\text{CH}_2\text{CH}_3$ (methoxypropane) and $\text{CH}_3\text{CH}_2\text{OCH}_2\text{CH}_3$ (ethoxyethane) have the same polyvalent functional group ($-\text{O}-$) but different alkyl groups attached to it (methyl and propyl versus two ethyl groups). Thus, they are metamers.

Answer: $\text{CH}_3\text{OCH}_2\text{CH}_2\text{CH}_3$ and $\text{CH}_3\text{CH}_2\text{OCH}_2\text{CH}_3$

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: During Lassaigne's test, the elements present in an organic compound are converted from :
questions.solution:
In Lassaigne's test, an organic compound is fused with sodium metal. The elements present in the organic compound, such as nitrogen, sulphur, and halogens, are initially present in covalent form.

During the fusion process, these elements react with sodium to form ionic sodium salts. For example, nitrogen and carbon form sodium cyanide ($\text{NaCN}$), sulphur forms sodium sulphide ($\text{Na}_2\text{S}$), and halogens form sodium halides ($\text{NaX}$).

Therefore, the elements are converted from covalent form to ionic form.

Answer: covalent form to ionic form

questions.q: The correct IUPAC name of the following compound is :
questions.solution:
1. Identify the longest continuous carbon chain: The longest chain in the given structure contains $7$ carbon atoms. Therefore, the parent alkane is heptane.

2. Identify the substituents: There is an ethyl group ($\text{-CH}_2\text{CH}_3$) and a methyl group ($\text{-CH}_3$) attached to the main chain.

- Numbering from left to right gives the substituents at positions $3$ (ethyl) and $5$ (methyl).
- Numbering from right to left gives the substituents at positions $3$ (methyl) and $5$ (ethyl).

4. Apply the alphabetical rule: When two different numbering schemes give the same set of locants ($3, 5$), the lower number is assigned to the substituent that is cited first alphabetically. Since 'ethyl' comes before 'methyl', the ethyl group must get the lower number ($3$).

5. Formulate the name: Combining these parts, the correct IUPAC name is $3$-ethyl-$5$-methylheptane.

Answer: $3$-ethyl-$5$-methylheptane

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q:
Arrange the following compounds in the increasing order of polarity
A. CH$_3$CH$_2$OCH$_2$CH$_3$
B. CH$_3$CH$_2$OH
C. CH$_3$COCH$_3$
D. CH$_3$COOH
Choose the correct answer from the options given below.
questions.solution:
The polarity of organic compounds depends on the presence of polar bonds and their ability to form hydrogen bonds.

Diethyl ether (A) has C-O bonds but lacks hydrogen bonding capabilities, making it the least polar among the given compounds.

Acetone (C) contains a highly polar C=O double bond, making it more polar than ethers, but it cannot act as a hydrogen bond donor.

Ethanol (B) contains an -OH group, which allows it to form strong intermolecular hydrogen bonds, making it more polar than ketones.

Acetic acid (D) contains both a carbonyl group (C=O) and a hydroxyl group (-OH). This allows for extensive hydrogen bonding (often forming dimers), making it the most polar of the given compounds.

Therefore, the increasing order of polarity is A < C < B < D.

Answer: $\text{A}\lt \text{C}\lt \text{B}\lt \text{D}$

questions.q: Given are cyclohexanol (I), acetic acid (II), 2, 4, 6-trinitrophenol (III) and phenol (IV). In these, the order of decreasing acidic character will be
questions.solution:
Key Idea:- Higher the tendency to give a proton, higher is the acidic character, and tendency to lose a proton depends upon the stability of intermediate, ie, carbanion formed. 2, 4, 6-trinitrophenol after the loss of a proton gives 2,4,6-trinitrophenoxide ion which is stabilised by resonance, $-I$ effect and $-M$ effect, thus is most acidic among the given compounds. Phenol after losing a proton form phenoxide ion which is also stabilised by resonance, $-M$ and $-I$ effects but is less stabilised as compared to 2, 4, 6-trinitrophenoxide ions. Thus, it is less acidic as compared to 2 , 4, 6-trinitrophenol. $\left(\mathrm{CH}_3 \mathrm{COOH}\right)$ after losing a proton gives acetate
ion which is stabilised by only resonance. However, it is more resonance stabilised as compared to a phenoxide ion, thus more acidic as compared to phenol. 2,4 , 6-trinitrophenol, however, is more acidic than acetic acid due to the presence of three electron withdrawing $-\mathrm{NO}_2$ groups. Cyclohexanol gives an anion that is least stable among the given, thus, it is least acidic. Hence, the correct order of acidic strength is $2,4,6$-trinitrophenol > acetic acid > phenol > cyclohexanol \text { III }>\text { II }>\text { IV }>\text { I }

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: The correct order of increasing bond angles in the following triatomic species is
questions.solution:
Key Idea : As the number of lone pair of electrons increases, bond angle decreases.
$\mathrm{NO}_2^{+}$ion is isoelectronic with $\mathrm{CO}_2$ molecule. It is a linear ion and its central atom $\left(\mathrm{N}^{+}\right)$ undergoes $s p$-hybridisation, hence bond angle is $180^{\circ}$.
In $\mathrm{NO}_2^{-}$ion, $\mathrm{N}$-atom undergoes $s p^2$ hybridisation. The angle between hybrid orbital should be $120^{\circ}$ but one lone pair of electrons is lying on $\mathrm{N}$-atom, hence bond angle decreases to $115^{\circ}$.
In $\mathrm{NO}_2$ molecule, $\mathrm{N}$-atom has one unpaired electron in $s p^2$-hybrid orbital. The bond angle should be $120^{\circ}$ but actually it is $132^{\circ}$. It may be due to one unpaired electron in $s p^2$-hybrid orbital.
Therefore, the increasing order of bond angles is :

\underset{\left(115^{\circ}\right)}{\mathrm{NO}_2^{-}} < \underset{\left(132^{\circ}\right)}{\mathrm{NO}_2} < \underset{\left(180^{\circ}\right)}{\mathrm{NO}_{+}^{+}}

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: Which one of the following orders of acid strength is correct?
questions.solution:
Carboxylic acids are most acidic and alcohols are least acidic. Phenols are more acidic than alcohols but less acidic than carboxylic acids or carbonic acid. Thus, acidic strength order is
\(\mathrm{R}-\underset{\underset{}{||} \atop \LARGE {\mathrm{O}}}{\mathrm{C}}-\mathrm{OH}\gt \mathrm{H}-\mathrm{O}-\mathrm{H}\gt \mathrm{R}-\mathrm{O}-\mathrm{H}\gt \mathrm{H}-\mathrm{C} \equiv \mathrm{C}-\mathrm{H}\)
Related Theory
Acid strength increases with :
1. increasing electronegativity of the central atom: The more electronegative the central atom, the more electron drift occurs, polarizing the $\mathrm{O}-\mathrm{H}$ bond which makes it easier for the molecule to dissociate.
2. increasing oxidation number of the central atom: The higher the oxidation state of the central atom, the greater the number of oxygens attached to the central atom. Oxygen is a highly electronegative element, contributing to greater electron drift away from the $\mathrm{O}-\mathrm{H}$ bond.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q:
Which of the following statements are correct?
(i) Inductive effect and resonance effect is possible in chlorobenzene.
(ii) Resonance effect dominates over inductive effect in anisole.
(iii) $p$-nitrobenzoic acid is less acidic than $m$-nitrobenzoic acid.
(iv) Diphenylamine is more basic than aniline.
questions.solution:
(i) The $\mathrm{Cl}$ group activates benzene ring more by resonance effect. $\mathrm{Cl}$ group being more electronegative withdraws electrons from benzene ring and shows - I effect. (ii) The methyl group of ether can donate electrons through inductive effect that is not as strong as electron donation effect to the pi-system. So, resonance effect dominates over inductive effect in anisole.
(iii) $p$-nitrobenzoic acid is more acidic than $m$-nitrobenzoic acid. When both acids donate $\mathrm{H}^{+}$ from $-\mathrm{COOH}$ group, then $p$-nitrobenzoate is more stabilised due to $m$-effect of nitro group at meta position by deactivating the ring. So, statement (iii) is incorrect. (iv) Diphenylamine is less basic than aniline. The lone pair of $\mathrm{N}$-atom in diphenylamine is delocalised on two benzene rings due to which it is less available to donate resulting into decrease in basicity. In aniline, it is delocalised on one benzene ring, so lone pair is more available for donation. Hence, it is more basic. So, statement IV is incorrect.

questions.q: Explain why (CH<sub>3</sub>)<sub>3</sub>C<sup>+</sup>is more stable than CH<sub>3</sub>CH<sub>2</sub><sup>+</sup>?

questions.q: Why CH<sub>3</sub><sup>+</sup>is the least stable cation?

CH<sub>3</sub><sup>+</sup>is the least stable cation because it is a highly polar molecule with a positive charge on carbon, making it prone to nucleophilic attack.
CH<sub>3</sub><sup>+</sup>is the least stable cation because it has an incomplete valence shell.
questions.solution:
Correct Option is : (B)
In CH3+, vacant p orbital is perpendicular to the plane in which C-H bonds lie; hence cannot overlap with it. Thus, CH3+lacks hyperconjugative stability.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: What are electrophiles and nucleophiles ? Explain with examples.
options: Electrophiles are substances that donate electrons to other molecules, while nucleophiles are substances that accept electrons from other molecules. For example, hydrogen ions (H<sup>+</sup>) are electrophiles, and hydroxide ions (OH<sup>-</sup>) are nucleophiles.

Electrophiles are substances that accept electrons from other molecules/species, while nucleophiles are substances that donate electrons to other molecules. For example, bromine (BF<sub>3</sub>) is an electrophile, and ammonia (NH<sub>3</sub>) is a nucleophile.

Electrophiles are substances that are negatively charged and donate electrons, while nucleophiles are substances that are positively charged and accept electrons. For example, chloride ions (Cl<sup>-</sup>) are electrophiles, and sodium ions (Na<sup>+</sup>) are nucleophiles.

Electrophiles are only substances that are positively charged and accept electrons, while nucleophiles are only substances that are negatively charged and donate electrons. For example, oxygen gas (O<sub>2</sub>) is an electrophile, and carbon dioxide (BF<sub>3</sub>) is a nucleophile.
questions.solution:
Correct Option is : (B)
Electrophiles are substances that accept electrons from other molecules/species, while nucleophiles are substances that donate electrons to other molecules. For example, bromine (BF3) is an electrophile, and ammonia (NH3) is a nucleophile.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: What is the chemistry of Lassaigne’s test?
options: Lassaigne's test is a method for the detection of the presence of hydrogen ions (H<sup>+</sup>) in a given substance. It involves the reaction of the test substance with sodium metal [NA] to form sodium hydride (NaH), which is then treated with water (H<sub>2</sub>O) to produce hydrogen gas (H<sub>2</sub>). The evolved hydrogen gas is confirmed using a gas test.

Lassaigne's test is a qualitative test used to detect the presence of halogens (chlorine, bromine, and iodine) and nitrogen in organic compounds. The test involves fusing the organic compound with sodium metal [NA] to form sodium cyanide (NaCN) and sodium halides (NaX), where X represents a halogen. The fused mass is then dissolved in water, and the resulting solution is acidified with dilute nitric acid (HNO<sub>3</sub>) to liberate the respective halogen acids (HX). These liberated halogen acids are identified using specific chemical tests.

Lassaigne's test is a procedure for determining the presence of metals in a given sample. It involves heating the sample with sodium metal [NA] to form sodium compounds of the metals present. The resulting mixture is then extracted with water to dissolve the sodium compounds. The aqueous solution is acidified with dilute sulphuric acid (H<sub>2</sub>SO<sub>4</sub>) to precipitate the metal sulfides, which can be identified by their characteristic colours.

Lassaigne's test is a method for determining the presence of carbonate ions (CO<sub>3</sub><sup>2-</sup>) in a given substance. It involves the reaction of the test substance with sodium metal [NA] to form sodium carbonate (Na<sub>2</sub>CO<sub>3</sub>). The resulting sodium carbonate is then acidified with hydrochloric acid (HCl) to produce carbon dioxide gas (CO<sub>2</sub>), which is confirmed using a gas test.
questions.solution:
Correct Option is : (B)
Lassaigne's test is a qualitative test used to detect the presence of halogens (chlorine, bromine, and iodine) and nitrogen in organic compounds. questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q:
Given below are two statements: one is labelled as Assertion (A) and the other is labelled as Reason (R).

Assertion (A): tert-Butyl carbocation is highly stable compared to methyl carbocation.
Reason (R): Methyl groups cannot participate in the resonance (mesomeric) effect as they lack $\pi$ bonds or lone pairs of electrons.

In the light of the above statements, choose the most appropriate answer from the options given below:
options: Both (A) and (R) are correct and (R) is the correct explanation of (A)
Both (A) and (R) are correct but (R) is not the correct explanation of (A)
(A) is correct but (R) is not correct
(A) is not correct but (R) is correct
questions.solution:
Assertion (A) is correct: The tert-butyl carbocation, $(CH_3)_3C^{+}$, is a tertiary carbocation and is highly stable compared to the methyl carbocation, $CH_3^{+}$.

Reason (R) is correct: The resonance (mesomeric) effect involves the delocalization of $\pi$ electrons or lone pairs. Methyl groups ($-CH_3$) only have $\sigma$ bonds and lack $\pi$ bonds or lone pairs, so they cannot participate in resonance.

However, (R) is not the correct explanation of (A). The correct explanation for the high stability of the tert-butyl carbocation is that the three methyl groups stabilize the positive charge through hyperconjugation (due to the presence of 9 $\alpha$-hydrogens) and the $+I$ (inductive) effect.

Therefore, both (A) and (R) are correct, but (R) is not the correct explanation of (A).

Answer: Both (A) and (R) are correct but (R) is not the correct explanation of (A)

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q:
Match the elements detected in an organic compound (List-I) with the reagents used and the corresponding observation in their qualitative analysis (List-II).

List-I (Element)List-II (Reagent and Observation)
(A) Nitrogen(I) Sodium nitroprusside, violet colour
(B) Sulphur(II) Ammonium molybdate, yellow precipitate
(C) Halogen(III) $\mathrm{FeSO_4}$ followed by conc. $\mathrm{H_2SO_4}$, Prussian blue colour
(D) Phosphorus(IV) $\mathrm{AgNO_3}$ and $\mathrm{HNO_3}$, precipitate


Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
questions.solution:
In the qualitative analysis of organic compounds:

(A) Nitrogen is detected by boiling the sodium fusion extract with $\mathrm{FeSO_4}$ and then acidifying with concentrated $\mathrm{H_2SO_4}$, which yields a Prussian blue colour due to the formation of ferriferrocyanide.

(B) Sulphur is detected by adding sodium nitroprusside to the sodium fusion extract, resulting in a violet colour.

(C) Halogens are detected by acidifying the sodium fusion extract with $\mathrm{HNO_3}$ and adding $\mathrm{AgNO_3}$, which forms a precipitate (white, pale yellow, or yellow depending on the halogen).

(D) Phosphorus is detected by heating the compound with an oxidising agent (like sodium peroxide), boiling with $\mathrm{HNO_3}$, and adding ammonium molybdate to form a yellow precipitate of ammonium phosphomolybdate.

Therefore, the correct match is (A)-(III), (B)-(I), (C)-(IV), (D)-(II).

Answer: (A)-(III), (B)-(I), (C)-(IV), (D)-(II)

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: A chemist separates a mixture of two amino acids by spotting the extract on a special strip of paper and suspending it in a suitable solvent. As the solvent rises up the paper, the amino acids are separated based on their differential distribution. According to NCERT principles, which of the following correctly identifies the stationary phase and the broad category of this chromatographic technique?
options: Stationary phase: Water trapped in the paper ; Technique: Partition chromatography
Stationary phase: Cellulose of the paper ; Technique: Adsorption chromatography
Stationary phase: Cellulose of the paper ; Technique: Partition chromatography
Stationary phase: The rising solvent ; Technique: Partition chromatography
questions.solution:
The scenario describes paper chromatography, which is routinely used to separate mixtures like amino acids.

According to NCERT, paper chromatography is a specific type of partition chromatography, not adsorption chromatography. The separation occurs due to the continuous differential partitioning of components between a stationary phase and a mobile phase.

A common misconception is that the solid paper (cellulose) itself acts as the stationary phase. However, the chromatography paper contains water trapped within its cellulose network, and it is this trapped water that acts as the true stationary phase. The rising solvent acts as the mobile phase.

Answer: Stationary phase: Water trapped in the paper ; Technique: Partition chromatography

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q:
Match List-I with List-II.

List-I (Carbocation)List-II (Number of hyperconjugative structures)
(A) 1-Methylcyclopentyl cation(I) 4
(B) Cyclohexyl cation(II) 6
(C) 1-Ethylcyclohexyl cation(III) 7
(D) 2-Methylbutan-2-yl cation(IV) 8

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
questions.solution:
The number of hyperconjugative structures for an alkyl carbocation is equal to the number of $\alpha$-hydrogen atoms (hydrogen atoms attached to the $sp^3$ hybridized carbon atoms directly adjacent to the positively charged carbon).

(A) 1-Methylcyclopentyl cation: The positively charged carbon is attached to a methyl group (3 $\alpha$-H) and two $-\mathrm{CH}_2-$ groups of the cyclopentyl ring (2 + 2 = 4 $\alpha$-H). Total $\alpha$-H = 7.

(B) Cyclohexyl cation: The positively charged carbon is attached to two $-\mathrm{CH}_2-$ groups of the cyclohexyl ring (2 + 2 = 4 $\alpha$-H). Total $\alpha$-H = 4.

(C) 1-Ethylcyclohexyl cation: The positively charged carbon is attached to an ethyl group ($-\mathrm{CH}_2\mathrm{CH}_3$, which provides 2 $\alpha$-H) and two $-\mathrm{CH}_2-$ groups of the cyclohexyl ring (2 + 2 = 4 $\alpha$-H). Total $\alpha$-H = 6.

(D) 2-Methylbutan-2-yl cation: The structure is $\mathrm{CH}_3-\stackrel{\oplus}{\mathrm{C}}(\mathrm{CH}_3)-\mathrm{CH}_2-\mathrm{CH}_3$. The positively charged carbon is attached to two methyl groups (3 + 3 = 6 $\alpha$-H) and one methylene group (2 $\alpha$-H). Total $\alpha$-H = 8.

Therefore, the correct matching is (A)-(III), (B)-(I), (C)-(II), (D)-(IV).

Answer: (A)-(III), (B)-(I), (C)-(II), (D)-(IV)

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: When optically active (S)-2-bromooctane is treated with aqueous NaOH, the reaction proceeds exclusively via an $\text{S}_{\text{N}}2$ mechanism. What will be the stereochemical nature of the major product formed and the optical activity of the resulting reaction mixture?
options: Racemic mixture of octan-2-ol, optically inactive
questions.solution:
The $\text{S}_{\text{N}}2$ reaction involves the attack of the incoming nucleophile ($\text{OH}^{-}$) from the side opposite to the leaving group ($\text{Br}^{-}$).

This back-side attack leads to a complete inversion of configuration at the chiral center. Therefore, the reactant (S)-2-bromooctane will be converted entirely into (R)-octan-2-ol.

Because only a single enantiomer is formed as the product, the resulting reaction mixture will be optically active.

A racemic mixture would only form if the reaction proceeded via an $\text{S}_{\text{N}}1$ mechanism. A meso compound is impossible here because octan-2-ol has only one chiral center.

Answer: (R)-octan-2-ol, optically active

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q:
Consider a six-membered cyclic organic compound containing a ketone group and one carbon-carbon double bond. The carbonyl carbon is directly attached to one of the carbons of the double bond. A bromine atom is attached to the other carbon of the double bond. Additionally, a methyl group is attached to the saturated side of the ring, separated from the carbonyl carbon by exactly one methylene ($-\text{CH}_2-$) group.

What is the correct IUPAC name of this compound?
questions.solution:
Based on the description, the structure is a substituted cyclohexenone ring.

The principal functional group is the ketone, so the carbonyl carbon is assigned the highest priority and designated as C-$1$.

Numbering must proceed around the ring to give the carbon-carbon double bond the lowest possible locants. Therefore, we number towards the double bond, making the double-bonded carbons C-$2$ and C-$3$.

The bromine atom is on the other carbon of the double bond, which places it at C-$3$.

The saturated side of the ring consists of C-$6$, C-$5$, and C-$4$. The methyl group is separated from C-$1$ by one methylene group (C-$6$), which places the methyl group at C-$5$.

The substituents are a bromo group at C-$3$ and a methyl group at C-$5$.

According to IUPAC rules, substituents are listed in alphabetical order as prefixes, so bromo precedes methyl.

Combining these parts, the correct IUPAC name is $3$-bromo-$5$-methylcyclohex-$2$-en-$1$-one.

Option 1 is incorrect because it numbers away from the double bond, violating the lowest locant rule for multiple bonds.

Option 2 is incorrect because it fails to give the principal functional group (ketone) the lowest locant.

Option 4 is incorrect because the substituents are not listed in alphabetical order.

Answer: $3$-bromo-$5$-methylcyclohex-$2$-en-$1$-one

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q:
What is the correct IUPAC name for the compound given below?

$HC \equiv C - CH(CH_2CH_3) - CH_2 - CH(CH_3) - CH_2 - CH_3$
questions.solution:
The principal functional group is the alkyne (triple bond), so the longest carbon chain containing the triple bond is selected as the parent chain. Here, the longest chain has 7 carbon atoms, making it a heptane derivative.

Numbering must be done from the end closer to the triple bond to give it the lowest possible locant. Thus, numbering starts from left to right, placing the triple bond at C1.

The substituents are an ethyl group at C3 and a methyl group at C5.

According to IUPAC rules, substituents are cited in alphabetical order. Ethyl comes before methyl.

Combining these parts, the correct IUPAC name is 3-Ethyl-5-methylhept-1-yne.

Answer: 3-Ethyl-5-methylhept-1-yne

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q:
Given below are two statements: one is labelled as Assertion (A) and the other is labelled as Reason (R).

Assertion (A): The cycloheptatrienyl (tropylium) cation is exceptionally stable compared to typical alkyl carbocations.
Reason (R): It contains six $\pi$ electrons delocalized over a non-planar seven-membered ring, which makes it aromatic.

In the light of the above statements, choose the most appropriate answer from the options given below:
options: Both (A) and (R) are true and (R) is the correct explanation of (A).
Both (A) and (R) are true but (R) is not the correct explanation of (A).
questions.solution:
Assertion (A) is true. The cycloheptatrienyl (tropylium) cation is exceptionally stable because it is an aromatic carbocation.

Reason (R) is false. While the tropylium cation does contain six $\pi$ electrons ($4n+2$ where $n=1$), a strict requirement for aromaticity according to Hückel's rule is that the ring must be planar to allow for continuous delocalization of the $\pi$ electrons. The reason incorrectly states that the ring is non-planar.

Therefore, (A) is true but (R) is false.

Answer: (A) is true but (R) is false.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q:
How many of the following compounds exhibit geometrical isomerism?
(I) But-2-ene
(II) 1,1-Dichloroethene
(III) 1,3-Dimethylcyclopentane
(IV) 2-Methylbut-2-ene
(V) 1,2-Dimethylcyclohexane
questions.solution:
For geometrical isomerism (GI) in alkenes, each carbon atom of the double bond must be bonded to two different atoms or groups.
For GI in cycloalkanes, at least two $\mathrm{sp}^3$ hybridized ring carbons must each be bonded to two different atoms or groups.

(I) But-2-ene: $\mathrm{CH_3-CH=CH-CH_3}$. Each double-bonded carbon is attached to a hydrogen atom and a methyl group. It exhibits GI.

(II) 1,1-Dichloroethene: $\mathrm{CCl_2=CH_2}$. One double-bonded carbon is attached to two identical chlorine atoms. It does not exhibit GI.

(III) 1,3-Dimethylcyclopentane: Two $\mathrm{sp}^3$ carbons (C1 and C3) are each attached to a hydrogen atom and a methyl group. It exhibits GI.

(IV) 2-Methylbut-2-ene: $\mathrm{(CH_3)_2C=CH-CH_3}$. One double-bonded carbon is attached to two identical methyl groups. It does not exhibit GI.

(V) 1,2-Dimethylcyclohexane: Two $\mathrm{sp}^3$ carbons (C1 and C2) are each attached to a hydrogen atom and a methyl group. It exhibits GI.

Thus, compounds (I), (III), and (V) exhibit geometrical isomerism. The total count is 3.

Answer: 3

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q:
Consider the following nitrogenous bases:
Aniline, Ammonia, Methylamine, and Dimethylamine.

Which of the following represents the correct decreasing order of their $\text{p}K_b$ values in aqueous solution?
questions.solution:
The basic strength of amines depends on the availability of the lone pair on the nitrogen atom for protonation.

In aqueous solution, aliphatic amines are stronger bases than ammonia due to the $+\text{I}$ effect of alkyl groups. Among methylamines, dimethylamine is a stronger base than methylamine due to a combination of $+\text{I}$ effect, solvation, and steric factors.

Aniline is a weaker base than ammonia because the lone pair on nitrogen is delocalised into the benzene ring through resonance.

Thus, the decreasing order of basic strength ($K_b$) is:
$\left(\text{CH}_3\right)_2\text{NH} \gt \text{CH}_3\text{NH}_2 \gt \text{NH}_3 \gt \text{C}_6\text{H}_5\text{NH}_2$

Since $\text{p}K_b = -\log K_b$, a stronger base has a lower $\text{p}K_b$ value. Therefore, the decreasing order of $\text{p}K_b$ values is the exact reverse of the basic strength order:
$\text{C}_6\text{H}_5\text{NH}_2 \gt \text{NH}_3 \gt \text{CH}_3\text{NH}_2 \gt \left(\text{CH}_3\right)_2\text{NH}$

Answer: $\text{C}_6\text{H}_5\text{NH}_2 \gt \text{NH}_3 \gt \text{CH}_3\text{NH}_2 \gt \left(\text{CH}_3\right)_2\text{NH}$

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q:
Read the following statements carefully:
(I) Steam distillation is used to purify substances which are steam volatile and miscible with water.
(II) Distillation under reduced pressure is used to purify liquids having very high boiling points and those which decompose at or below their boiling points.
(III) A fractionating column provides many surfaces for heat exchange between the ascending vapours and the descending condensed liquid.
(IV) Simple distillation is suitable for separating a mixture of liquids whose boiling points differ by less than $10\text{ K}$.

How many of the above statements are correct?
questions.solution:
Statement (I) is incorrect because steam distillation is applied to separate substances which are steam volatile and are immiscible with water, not miscible.

Statement (II) is correct as distillation under reduced pressure (vacuum distillation) lowers the boiling point, preventing decomposition of high-boiling liquids.

Statement (III) is correct because the fractionating column provides a large surface area for repeated vaporization and condensation, facilitating the separation of close-boiling liquids.

Statement (IV) is incorrect because simple distillation is used for liquids with a large difference in boiling points. For liquids with a boiling point difference of less than $10\text{ K}$, fractional distillation is required.

Therefore, only two statements, (II) and (III), are correct.

Answer: Only two

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: Which of the following compounds is a metamer of pentan-2-one?
questions.solution:
Pentan-2-one ($\text{CH}_3-\text{CO}-\text{CH}_2\text{CH}_2\text{CH}_3$) has a methyl group and an n-propyl group attached to the polyvalent carbonyl ($-\text{CO}-$) group.

Metamerism arises due to different alkyl chains on either side of the polyvalent functional group in the molecule.

Pentan-3-one ($\text{CH}_3\text{CH}_2-\text{CO}-\text{CH}_2\text{CH}_3$) has two ethyl groups attached to the carbonyl group. Since the distribution of alkyl groups around the functional group is different, it is a metamer of pentan-2-one.

3-Methylbutan-2-one has a different principal carbon chain length (4 carbons instead of 5), making it primarily a chain isomer.

Pentanal is an aldehyde, which makes it a functional isomer.

Pentan-2-ol is an alcohol with a different molecular formula ($\text{C}_5\text{H}_{12}\text{O}$ instead of $\text{C}_5\text{H}_{10}\text{O}$).

Answer: Pentan-3-one
