(C) Pentane and 2-methylbutane(III) Functional isomerism
(D) Ethanol and methoxymethane(IV) Metamerism


Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
questions.solution:
(A) Pentan-2-one ($\text{CH}_3-\text{CO}-\text{CH}_2\text{CH}_2\text{CH}_3$) and Pentan-3-one ($\text{CH}_3\text{CH}_2-\text{CO}-\text{CH}_2\text{CH}_3$) have different alkyl groups attached to the polyvalent carbonyl group ($-\text{CO}-$), so they exhibit metamerism. (A)-(IV).

(B) But-1-yne and But-2-yne differ in the position of the carbon-carbon triple bond, making them position isomers. (B)-(II).

(C) Pentane and 2-methylbutane have different carbon skeletons, classifying them as chain isomers. (C)-(I).

(D) Ethanol is an alcohol ($-\text{OH}$) and methoxymethane is an ether ($-\text{O}-$). They possess different functional groups and are functional isomers. (D)-(III).

Thus, the correct matching is (A)-(IV), (B)-(II), (C)-(I), (D)-(III).

Answer: (A)-(IV), (B)-(II), (C)-(I), (D)-(III)

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: Which of the following alkylbenzenes does NOT exhibit hyperconjugation with the benzene ring?
questions.solution:
Hyperconjugation in alkylarenes requires the presence of at least one $\alpha$-hydrogen on the $sp^3$ hybridized carbon directly attached to the $sp^2$ carbon of the aromatic ring.

In tert-butylbenzene, the carbon atom attached to the benzene ring is bonded to three methyl groups and has no $\alpha$-hydrogen. Therefore, it does not exhibit hyperconjugation.

Toluene has three $\alpha$-hydrogens, ethylbenzene has two $\alpha$-hydrogens, and isopropylbenzene has one $\alpha$-hydrogen, allowing them to show hyperconjugation.

Answer: tert-Butylbenzene

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: Which of the following compounds will undergo heterolytic cleavage of the C-Br bond most readily?
questions.solution:
The ease of heterolytic cleavage of a C-Br bond depends directly on the stability of the carbocation formed after the departure of the bromide ion.

Let us analyze the carbocations formed from each compound:

1) Bromobenzene forms a phenyl cation, which is highly unstable as the positive charge resides on an $sp^2$ hybridized carbon atom.

2) 3-Bromopropene forms an allyl cation ($CH_2=CH-CH_2^+$), which is a $1^\circ$ carbocation stabilized by resonance.

3) 1-Bromo-1-phenylethane forms a $2^\circ$ benzylic cation ($C_6H_5-C^+H-CH_3$). This cation is highly stabilized by extensive resonance delocalization over the benzene ring as well as hyperconjugation from the adjacent methyl group.

4) 1-Bromopropane forms a $1^\circ$ alkyl cation ($CH_3-CH_2-CH_2^+$), which is stabilized only by hyperconjugation (2 $\alpha$-hydrogens).

Since the $2^\circ$ benzylic cation is the most stable intermediate among the choices, 1-bromo-1-phenylethane undergoes heterolytic cleavage most readily.

Answer: 1-Bromo-1-phenylethane

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: An organic compound containing both nitrogen and sulphur is fused with a large excess of sodium metal. The resulting Lassaigne's extract is then treated with neutral $\text{FeCl}_3$ solution. What is the expected observation and the chemical reason for it?
options: A blood-red colour is observed because sodium thiocyanate is highly stable and forms a complex with $\text{Fe}^{3+}$.
A blood-red colour is observed because excess sodium accelerates the formation of the $[\text{Fe}(\text{SCN})]^{2+}$ complex.
No blood-red colour is observed because excess sodium decomposes sodium thiocyanate into sodium cyanide and sodium sulphide.
A Prussian blue colour is observed immediately because excess sodium directly converts the thiocyanate ion into $[\text{Fe}(\text{CN})_6]^{4-}$.
questions.solution:
When an organic compound containing both nitrogen and sulphur is fused with sodium metal, sodium thiocyanate ($\text{NaSCN}$) is initially formed.

However, if the fusion is carried out with a large excess of sodium metal, the sodium thiocyanate decomposes to yield sodium cyanide and sodium sulphide:
$\text{NaSCN} + 2\text{Na} \rightarrow \text{NaCN} + \text{Na}_2\text{S}$

Because the thiocyanate ion ($\text{SCN}^{-}$) is destroyed, the extract will not give the characteristic blood-red colour of the $[\text{Fe}(\text{SCN})]^{2+}$ complex when treated with neutral $\text{FeCl}_3$. Instead, the cyanide and sulphide ions will give their usual independent tests if treated with appropriate reagents.

Answer: No blood-red colour is observed because excess sodium decomposes sodium thiocyanate into sodium cyanide and sodium sulphide.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: An organic compound containing both nitrogen and sulphur is fused with an excess of sodium metal to prepare Lassaigne's extract. Which of the following ionic species will be predominantly present in the resulting extract for detection?
questions.solution:
Normally, when an organic compound containing both nitrogen and sulphur is fused with sodium, sodium thiocyanate ($\text{NaSCN}$) is formed, which provides the thiocyanate ion ($\text{SCN}^{-}$).

However, when an excess of sodium metal is used during the fusion process, the sodium thiocyanate decomposes to form sodium cyanide and sodium sulphide.
$\text{NaSCN} + 2\text{Na} \rightarrow \text{NaCN} + \text{Na}_{2}\text{S}$

As a result, the extract will predominantly contain cyanide ($\text{CN}^{-}$) and sulphide ($\text{S}^{2-}$) ions instead of thiocyanate ions.

Answer: Cyanide ($\text{CN}^{-}$) and Sulphide ($\text{S}^{2-}$) ions

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q:
Match List I with List II.

(A)$CH_3-CH(Br)-CH_2-CH(Cl)-CH(Cl)-CH_3$(I)2-ethylpentan-1-ol
(B)$CH_3-CH_2-CH_2-CH(CH_2OH)-CH_2-CH_3$(II)4-hydroxypentan-2-one
(C)$CH_3-CO-CH_2-CH(OH)-CH_3$(III)pent-1-en-4-yne
(D)$CH_2=CH-CH_2-C \equiv CH$(IV)5-bromo-2,3-dichlorohexane

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
questions.solution:
(A) $CH_3-CH(Br)-CH_2-CH(Cl)-CH(Cl)-CH_3$: Numbering from right to left gives locants 2, 3, 5. Numbering from left to right gives 2, 4, 5. The lowest locant set is 2, 3, 5. Substituents are listed alphabetically. The name is 5-bromo-2,3-dichlorohexane. Matches with (IV).

(B) $CH_3-CH_2-CH_2-CH(CH_2OH)-CH_2-CH_3$: The principal functional group is -OH. The parent chain must include the carbon attached to the -OH group, even if it is not the longest continuous chain in the molecule. The longest chain containing the -OH group has 5 carbons. Numbering starts from the -OH end. The name is 2-ethylpentan-1-ol. Matches with (I).

(C) $CH_3-CO-CH_2-CH(OH)-CH_3$: The ketone group has higher priority than the alcohol group. Numbering starts from the left to give the ketone the lowest locant (2). The name is 4-hydroxypentan-2-one. Matches with (II).

(D) $CH_2=CH-CH_2-C \equiv CH$: Numbering from either side gives locants 1 and 4 for the multiple bonds. In case of a tie, the double bond gets priority for the lower locant. Numbering is from left to right. The name is pent-1-en-4-yne. Matches with (III).

Therefore, the correct matching is (A)-(IV), (B)-(I), (C)-(II), (D)-(III).

Answer: (A)-(IV), (B)-(I), (C)-(II), (D)-(III)

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: Which of the following alkyl free radicals is the most stable?
questions.solution:
The stability of alkyl free radicals is determined by hyperconjugation, which depends on the number of $\alpha$-hydrogen atoms attached to the $sp^3$ hybridized carbon atoms adjacent to the radical center. Greater the number of $\alpha$-hydrogens, greater is the number of hyperconjugative structures, and hence more stable is the free radical.

Let us count the $\alpha$-hydrogens for each option:
1) $\left(\mathrm{CH}_3\right)_3\mathrm{C}-\overset{\bullet}{\mathrm{C}}\mathrm{H}_2$ has 0 $\alpha$-hydrogens.
2) $\mathrm{CH}_3-\mathrm{CH}_2-\overset{\bullet}{\mathrm{C}}\mathrm{H}-\mathrm{CH}_2-\mathrm{CH}_3$ has 4 $\alpha$-hydrogens.
3) $\mathrm{CH}_3-\overset{\bullet}{\mathrm{C}}\mathrm{H}-\mathrm{CH}_2-\mathrm{CH}_2-\mathrm{CH}_3$ has 5 $\alpha$-hydrogens.
4) $\mathrm{CH}_3-\overset{\bullet}{\mathrm{C}}\mathrm{H}-\mathrm{CH}_3$ has 6 $\alpha$-hydrogens.

Since $\mathrm{CH}_3-\overset{\bullet}{\mathrm{C}}\mathrm{H}-\mathrm{CH}_3$ has the maximum number of $\alpha$-hydrogens (6), it is the most stable free radical.

Answer: $\mathrm{CH}_3-\overset{\bullet}{\mathrm{C}}\mathrm{H}-\mathrm{CH}_3$

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q:
Match List-I with List-II regarding Lassaigne's test for organic compounds:

List-I (Elements present)List-II (Observation)
(A) Nitrogen(I) Blood red colour with $\text{Fe}^{3+}$
(B) Sulphur(II) Violet colour with sodium nitroprusside
(C) Both Nitrogen and Sulphur(III) Prussian blue colour with $\text{FeSO}_4$ and conc. $\text{H}_2\text{SO}_4$
(D) Chlorine(IV) White precipitate with $\text{AgNO}_3$ soluble in $\text{NH}_4\text{OH}$

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
questions.solution:
In Lassaigne's test for organic compounds:

Nitrogen forms sodium cyanide ($\text{NaCN}$), which reacts with $\text{FeSO}_4$ and conc. $\text{H}_2\text{SO}_4$ to give a Prussian blue colour of $\text{Fe}_4[\text{Fe}(\text{CN})_6]_3$.

Sulphur forms sodium sulphide ($\text{Na}_2\text{S}$), which gives a violet colour with sodium nitroprusside due to the formation of $[\text{Fe}(\text{CN})_5\text{NOS}]^{4-}$.

When both Nitrogen and Sulphur are present, sodium thiocyanate ($\text{NaSCN}$) is formed, which gives a blood red colour with $\text{Fe}^{3+}$ ions due to the formation of $[\text{Fe}(\text{SCN})]^{2+}$.

Chlorine forms sodium chloride ($\text{NaCl}$), which reacts with $\text{AgNO}_3$ to give a white precipitate of $\text{AgCl}$ that is soluble in ammonium hydroxide.

Therefore, the correct matching is (A)-(III), (B)-(II), (C)-(I), (D)-(IV).

Answer: (A)-(III), (B)-(II), (C)-(I), (D)-(IV)

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: An organic compound containing nitrogen is fused with sodium metal. The resulting sodium fusion extract is boiled with iron(II) sulphate and then acidified with concentrated sulphuric acid. The formation of a Prussian blue colour confirms the presence of nitrogen. What is the exact chemical formula of the complex responsible for this Prussian blue colour?
questions.solution:
During Lassaigne's test for nitrogen, the sodium fusion extract contains sodium cyanide ($\mathrm{NaCN}$). On boiling with iron(II) sulphate, sodium hexacyanidoferrate(II), $\mathrm{Na}_4[\mathrm{Fe}(\mathrm{CN})_6]$, is formed.

Upon adding concentrated sulphuric acid, some iron(II) is oxidised to iron(III), which reacts with the sodium hexacyanidoferrate(II) to produce iron(III) hexacyanidoferrate(II), $\mathrm{Fe}_4[\mathrm{Fe}(\mathrm{CN})_6]_3 \cdot x\mathrm{H}_2\mathrm{O}$. This complex is responsible for the Prussian blue colour.

The distractor $\mathrm{Fe}_3[\mathrm{Fe}(\mathrm{CN})_6]_4$ has incorrect valencies for the iron atoms inside and outside the coordination sphere. $\mathrm{Na}_4[\mathrm{Fe}(\mathrm{CN})_6]$ is the intermediate complex, and $[\mathrm{Fe}(\mathrm{SCN})]^{2+}$ is the species responsible for the blood-red colour when both nitrogen and sulphur are present.

Answer: $\mathrm{Fe}_4[\mathrm{Fe}(\mathrm{CN})_6]_3 \cdot x\mathrm{H}_2\mathrm{O}$

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: Which of the following compounds exhibits both geometrical isomerism and optical isomerism?
questions.solution:
To exhibit both geometrical and optical isomerism, a molecule must have a double bond capable of showing cis-trans isomerism and a chiral center.

3-Chloropent-2-ene ($\mathrm{CH}_3-\mathrm{CH}=\mathrm{C}(\mathrm{Cl})-\mathrm{CH}_2-\mathrm{CH}_3$): The double bond has different groups on each carbon, so it shows geometrical isomerism. However, it lacks an $\mathrm{sp}^3$ carbon with four different groups, so it does not show optical isomerism.

4-Chloro-2-methylpent-2-ene ($(\mathrm{CH}_3)_2\mathrm{C}=\mathrm{CH}-\mathrm{CH}(\mathrm{Cl})-\mathrm{CH}_3$): C-2 is attached to two identical methyl groups, so it does not show geometrical isomerism. C-4 is a chiral center, so it shows optical isomerism.

2-Chlorobut-2-ene ($\mathrm{CH}_3-\mathrm{C}(\mathrm{Cl})=\mathrm{CH}-\mathrm{CH}_3$): Shows geometrical isomerism but lacks a chiral center.

4-Chloropent-2-ene ($\mathrm{CH}_3-\mathrm{CH}=\mathrm{CH}-\mathrm{CH}(\mathrm{Cl})-\mathrm{CH}_3$): The double bond (C-2=C-3) has different groups attached to each carbon ($\mathrm{H}$ and $\mathrm{CH}_3$ on C-2; $\mathrm{H}$ and $-\mathrm{CH}(\mathrm{Cl})\mathrm{CH}_3$ on C-3), allowing for geometrical isomerism. Additionally, C-4 is a chiral center as it is attached to four different groups ($-\mathrm{H}$, $-\mathrm{Cl}$, $-\mathrm{CH}_3$, and $-\mathrm{CH}=\mathrm{CH}-\mathrm{CH}_3$). Thus, it exhibits both geometrical and optical isomerism.

Answer: 4-Chloropent-2-ene

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: Which of the following pairs of molecules represents metamers?
questions.solution:
Metamerism arises due to different alkyl chains on either side of a polyvalent functional group.

Propan-1-amine and propan-2-amine differ in the position of the $-\text{NH}_2$ group, making them position isomers.

Butan-1-amine and 2-methylpropan-1-amine have different carbon skeletons, making them chain isomers.

N-methylethanamine is a secondary amine, while propan-1-amine is a primary amine. They have different functional groups (secondary vs primary amine) and are functional isomers.

N-ethylethanamine ($\text{CH}_3\text{CH}_2-\text{NH}-\text{CH}_2\text{CH}_3$) and N-methylpropan-1-amine ($\text{CH}_3-\text{NH}-\text{CH}_2\text{CH}_2\text{CH}_3$) have the same polyvalent functional group ($-\text{NH}-$) but different alkyl groups attached to it (two ethyl groups versus one methyl and one propyl group). Therefore, they are metamers.

Answer: N-ethylethanamine and N-methylpropan-1-amine

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q:
Consider the following carbocations:
(I) $\left(\mathrm{CH}_3\right)_3\overset{\oplus}{\mathrm{C}}$
(II) $\mathrm{CH}_2=\mathrm{CH}-\overset{\oplus}{\mathrm{C}}\mathrm{H}_2$
(III) $\left(\mathrm{CH}_3\right)_2\overset{\oplus}{\mathrm{C}}\mathrm{H}$
(IV) $\mathrm{CH}_2=\overset{\oplus}{\mathrm{C}}\mathrm{H}$

The correct decreasing order of their stability is:
questions.solution:
The stability of carbocations depends on resonance, hyperconjugation, and the hybridization of the carbon bearing the positive charge.

(I) $\left(\mathrm{CH}_3\right)_3\overset{\oplus}{\mathrm{C}}$ (tert-butyl cation) is highly stabilized by hyperconjugation due to 9 $\alpha$-hydrogens.
(II) $\mathrm{CH}_2=\mathrm{CH}-\overset{\oplus}{\mathrm{C}}\mathrm{H}_2$ (allyl cation) is stabilized by resonance involving the adjacent $\pi$ bond.
(III) $\left(\mathrm{CH}_3\right)_2\overset{\oplus}{\mathrm{C}}\mathrm{H}$ (isopropyl cation) is stabilized by hyperconjugation from 6 $\alpha$-hydrogens.
(IV) $\mathrm{CH}_2=\overset{\oplus}{\mathrm{C}}\mathrm{H}$ (vinyl cation) is highly unstable because the positive charge is on an electronegative $sp$ hybridized carbon atom.

Although resonance generally provides strong stabilization, the hyperconjugation from 9 $\alpha$-hydrogens in the tert-butyl cation makes it more stable than the primary allyl cation. The allyl cation is more stable than the isopropyl cation ($2^\circ$). The vinyl cation is the least stable. Thus, the correct decreasing order of stability is (I) > (II) > (III) > (IV).

Answer: (I) > (II) > (III) > (IV)

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: In the qualitative analysis of an organic compound, the sample is strongly heated with dry copper(II) oxide in a hard glass tube. Which of the following element(s) in the organic compound are detected using this specific method?
questions.solution:
Carbon and hydrogen in an organic compound are detected by heating the compound with copper(II) oxide (CuO).

During this process, the carbon present in the compound is oxidised to carbon dioxide (which turns lime water milky) and the hydrogen is oxidised to water (which turns anhydrous copper sulphate blue).

Nitrogen, sulphur, halogens, and phosphorus are detected by preparing a sodium fusion extract (Lassaigne's test), not by heating with CuO.

Answer: Carbon and Hydrogen

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: It is observed that 2,3-dimethylbut-2-ene is significantly more stable than but-2-ene. Which of the following electronic effects is primarily responsible for this difference in stability?
questions.solution:
The stability of alkenes increases with the number of alkyl groups attached to the double-bonded carbon atoms. These alkyl groups stabilize the alkene primarily through hyperconjugation, which involves the delocalization of $\sigma$-electrons of the $\alpha$-C-H bonds into the empty $\pi^{*}$ antibonding orbital of the adjacent double bond.

2,3-dimethylbut-2-ene has 12 $\alpha$-hydrogens, leading to 12 hyperconjugative structures, whereas but-2-ene has only 6 $\alpha$-hydrogens. While the $+I$ effect is also present, hyperconjugation is a stronger and more dominant stabilizing factor for alkenes.

Answer: Hyperconjugation

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: Which of the following carbocations is the most stable?
questions.solution:
The stability of carbocations is determined by the electron-donating effects (resonance, hyperconjugation, and inductive effects) of the attached groups.

1) The tert-butyl cation, $(CH_3)_3C^+$, is a $3^\circ$ carbocation stabilized by hyperconjugation involving 9 $\alpha$-hydrogens.

2) The methoxymethyl cation, $CH_3-O-CH_2^+$, is stabilized by the +M (resonance) effect of the oxygen atom. The lone pair on oxygen is donated to the empty p-orbital of the carbocation, forming a pi bond ($CH_3-O^+=CH_2$). This completes the octet of every atom, providing exceptional stability that generally outweighs hyperconjugation or simple pi-bond resonance.

3) The allyl cation, $CH_2=CH-CH_2^+$, is stabilized by resonance with the adjacent pi bond, but the positively charged carbon atom still has an incomplete octet in its resonance structures.

4) The isopropyl cation, $(CH_3)_2CH^+$, is a $2^\circ$ carbocation stabilized by hyperconjugation (6 $\alpha$-hydrogens).

Therefore, the methoxymethyl cation is the most stable due to octet completion via the +M effect.

Answer: $CH_3-O-CH_2^+$

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q:
Consider the following statements regarding hyperconjugation:

(I) It is a permanent electronic effect.
(II) It involves the delocalization of $\sigma$ electrons.
(III) It is also known as no-bond resonance.
(IV) In carbocations, it involves the overlap of a C-H $\sigma$ bond with an empty p-orbital.

How many of the above statements are correct?
questions.solution:
Statement (I) is correct: Hyperconjugation is a permanent effect, unlike the electromeric effect which is temporary.

Statement (II) is correct: It involves the delocalization of $\sigma$ electrons of a C-H bond of an alkyl group directly attached to an atom of an unsaturated system or to an atom with an unshared p-orbital.

Statement (III) is correct: Since there is no bond between the alpha-carbon and the hydrogen atom in some of the contributing resonance structures, it is also known as no-bond resonance.

Statement (IV) is correct: In carbocations (e.g., ethyl cation), the empty p-orbital of the positively charged carbon overlaps with the $\sigma$ electrons of the adjacent C-H bond.

Therefore, all four statements are correct.

Answer: All four

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: During an organic reaction, a temporary effect involving the complete transfer of a shared pair of $\pi$-electrons to one of the atoms joined by a multiple bond operates in the opposite direction to a permanent effect involving the fractional polarisation of $\sigma$-bonds. Identify the two effects and the one that predominates.
options: Temporary effect is the resonance effect, permanent effect is the inductive effect; the resonance effect predominates.
Temporary effect is the electromeric effect, permanent effect is the inductive effect; the electromeric effect predominates.
Temporary effect is the electromeric effect, permanent effect is the inductive effect; the inductive effect predominates.
Temporary effect is the electromeric effect, permanent effect is hyperconjugation; the electromeric effect predominates.
questions.solution:
The temporary effect involving the complete transfer of a shared pair of $\pi$-electrons to one of the atoms joined by a multiple bond at the requirement of an attacking reagent is the electromeric effect.

The permanent effect involving the fractional polarisation of $\sigma$-bonds due to a difference in electronegativity is the inductive effect.

According to NCERT, when the inductive and electromeric effects operate in opposite directions, the temporary electromeric effect predominates over the permanent inductive effect.

Answer: Temporary effect is the electromeric effect, permanent effect is the inductive effect; the electromeric effect predominates.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: In order to detect elements such as nitrogen, sulphur, and halogens in an organic compound, their covalent bonds must be broken to convert them into water-soluble ionic species. Which of the following laboratory processes is specifically used to achieve this conversion for qualitative analysis?
questions.solution:
In qualitative analysis of organic compounds, elements like nitrogen, sulphur, and halogens are covalently bonded. To detect them, they must be converted into their ionic forms.

This is achieved by fusing the organic compound with sodium metal, a process known as sodium fusion or Lassaigne's test. The covalent compounds are converted into water-soluble ionic sodium salts (such as $\text{NaCN}$, $\text{Na}_2\text{S}$, and $\text{NaX}$).

Kjeldahl's and Dumas methods are used for the quantitative estimation of nitrogen, while the Carius method is used for the quantitative estimation of halogens and sulphur.

Answer: Sodium fusion (Lassaigne's test)

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q:
Given below are two statements: one is labelled as Assertion (A) and the other is labelled as Reason (R).

Assertion (A): During steam distillation, the organic liquid boils at a temperature lower than its normal boiling point.
Reason (R): The organic liquid boils when the sum of its vapour pressure and the vapour pressure of water becomes equal to the atmospheric pressure.

In the light of the above statements, choose the most appropriate answer from the options given below:
options: Both Assertion (A) and Reason (R) are true but Reason (R) is not the correct explanation of Assertion (A)
Assertion (A) is true but Reason (R) is false
Both Assertion (A) and Reason (R) are true and Reason (R) is the correct explanation of Assertion (A)
Assertion (A) is false but Reason (R) is true
questions.solution:
In steam distillation, a mixture of steam and the volatile organic compound is vaporised. The mixture boils when the sum of the vapour pressures of the organic liquid ($p_1$) and water ($p_2$) becomes equal to the atmospheric pressure ($p$), i.e., $p = p_1 + p_2$.

Since the partial vapour pressure of the organic liquid ($p_1$) is less than the total atmospheric pressure ($p$), the organic liquid reaches its required partial pressure at a lower temperature than its normal boiling point. Consequently, it vaporises at a lower temperature.

Therefore, both Assertion (A) and Reason (R) are true, and Reason (R) is the correct explanation of Assertion (A).

Answer: Both Assertion (A) and Reason (R) are true and Reason (R) is the correct explanation of Assertion (A)

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: Which of the following condensed structural formulas correctly represents $4$-bromo-$3$-methylpentan-$2$-ol?
questions.solution:
The root word pentan indicates a parent chain of $5$ carbon atoms.

The suffix -$2$-ol indicates that the principal functional group, the hydroxyl ($-\text{OH}$) group, is located at carbon-$2$.

The prefixes $4$-bromo and $3$-methyl indicate a bromine atom at carbon-$4$ and a methyl group at carbon-$3$.

Analyzing the given options:

Option 1 has a $5$-carbon chain. Numbering from left to right gives the $-\text{OH}$ group the lowest locant ($2$). The substituents are $3$-bromo and $4$-methyl, making its IUPAC name $3$-bromo-$4$-methylpentan-$2$-ol.

Option 2 has a $5$-carbon chain. Numbering from right to left gives the $-\text{OH}$ group the lowest locant ($2$). The methyl group is at C-$3$ and the bromo group is at C-$4$. This exactly matches $4$-bromo-$3$-methylpentan-$2$-ol.

Option 3 has a $6$-carbon parent chain, making it a hexanol ($5$-bromo-$4$-methylhexan-$2$-ol).

Option 4 has the bromo group at the end of the chain, making its IUPAC name $5$-bromo-$3$-methylpentan-$2$-ol.

Answer: $\text{CH}_3-\text{CH}(\text{Br})-\text{CH}(\text{CH}_3)-\text{CH}(\text{OH})-\text{CH}_3$

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q:
Consider the following physical properties of four hypothetical organic liquids P, Q, S, and T:
Liquid P: Boiling point $350\text{ K}$, miscible with Q.
Liquid Q: Boiling point $360\text{ K}$, miscible with P.
Liquid S: Boiling point $500\text{ K}$, decomposes at $480\text{ K}$.
Liquid T: Boiling point $457\text{ K}$, immiscible with water, steam volatile.

Based on the above data, choose the correct statement regarding their most appropriate purification techniques.
options: A mixture of P and Q is separated by simple distillation, and liquid S is purified by fractional distillation.
A mixture of T and water is separated by fractional distillation, and liquid S is purified by simple distillation.
A mixture of P and Q is separated by simple distillation, and a mixture of T and water is separated by steam distillation.
A mixture of P and Q is separated by fractional distillation, and liquid S is purified by distillation under reduced pressure.
questions.solution:
Liquids P and Q are miscible and have a boiling point difference of only $10\text{ K}$ ($360\text{ K} - 350\text{ K}$). Mixtures of miscible liquids with a small boiling point difference are separated using fractional distillation, not simple distillation.

Liquid S has a normal boiling point of $500\text{ K}$ but decomposes at $480\text{ K}$ (below its boiling point). Such liquids are purified by distillation under reduced pressure (vacuum distillation) to prevent thermal decomposition.

Liquid T is immiscible with water and is steam volatile, which are the exact conditions required for steam distillation.

Therefore, the statement correctly pairing the techniques is that a mixture of P and Q is separated by fractional distillation, and liquid S is purified by distillation under reduced pressure.

Answer: A mixture of P and Q is separated by fractional distillation, and liquid S is purified by distillation under reduced pressure.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q:
Match the elements present in an organic compound (List-I) with the specific ionic sodium salts they form in Lassaigne's extract (List-II).

List-I (Elements)List-II (Ionic sodium salts)
(A) Nitrogen(I) $\text{Na}_{2}\text{S}$
(B) Sulphur(II) $\text{NaSCN}$
(C) Halogen(III) $\text{NaCN}$
(D) Nitrogen and Sulphur both(IV) $\text{NaX}$

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
questions.solution:
In Lassaigne's test, the covalently bonded elements in an organic compound are fused with sodium metal to form water-soluble ionic sodium salts.

The specific reactions are:
Nitrogen forms sodium cyanide: $\text{Na} + \text{C} + \text{N} \rightarrow \text{NaCN}$
Sulphur forms sodium sulphide: $2\text{Na} + \text{S} \rightarrow \text{Na}_{2}\text{S}$
Halogens form sodium halides: $\text{Na} + \text{X} \rightarrow \text{NaX}$
When both Nitrogen and Sulphur are present, they form sodium thiocyanate: $\text{Na} + \text{C} + \text{N} + \text{S} \rightarrow \text{NaSCN}$

Therefore, the correct matching is (A)-(III), (B)-(I), (C)-(IV), and (D)-(II).

Answer: (A)-(III), (B)-(I), (C)-(IV), (D)-(II)

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q:
Given below are two statements: one is labelled as Assertion (A) and the other is labelled as Reason (R).

Assertion (A): A racemic mixture of butan-2-ol is optically inactive due to internal compensation.
Reason (R): A racemic mixture contains equal proportions of two enantiomers, and the optical rotation caused by one isomer is exactly cancelled by the other.

In the light of the above statements, choose the most appropriate answer from the options given below:
options: Both Assertion and Reason are correct and Reason is the correct explanation for Assertion.
Both Assertion and Reason are correct but Reason is not the correct explanation for Assertion.
Assertion is not correct but Reason is correct.
Assertion is correct but Reason is not correct.
questions.solution:
Assertion (A) is incorrect because a racemic mixture is optically inactive due to external compensation, not internal compensation. Internal compensation is the reason for the optical inactivity of meso compounds, where one half of the molecule cancels the optical rotation of the other half.

Reason (R) is correct as it accurately describes the composition of a racemic mixture. It contains a $1:1$ mixture of two enantiomers, meaning the rotation caused by the dextrorotatory isomer is exactly cancelled by the levorotatory isomer, leading to zero net optical rotation (external compensation).

Answer: Assertion is not correct but Reason is correct.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q:
Match List-I with List-II.

List-IList-II
(A) The permanent effect that is weaker than the electromeric effect when they operate in opposite directions(I) Electromeric effect
(B) Temporary complete transfer of $\pi$ electrons in the presence of an attacking reagent(II) Hyperconjugation
(C) Delocalisation of $\sigma$ electrons of a C-H bond into an adjacent $\pi$ system(III) Resonance effect
(D) Polarity produced in a molecule by the interaction of two $\pi$ bonds or a $\pi$ bond and lone pair(IV) Inductive effect

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
questions.solution:
(A) When the inductive and electromeric effects operate in opposite directions, the temporary electromeric effect predominates over the permanent inductive effect. Thus, (A) matches with Inductive effect (IV).

(B) The electromeric effect involves the temporary complete transfer of shared $\pi$ electrons to one of the atoms joined by a multiple bond on the demand of an attacking reagent. Thus, (B) matches with Electromeric effect (I).

(C) Hyperconjugation involves the delocalisation of $\sigma$ electrons of a C-H bond of an alkyl group directly attached to an atom of an unsaturated system or to an atom with an unshared $p$ orbital. Thus, (C) matches with Hyperconjugation (II).

(D) The resonance effect is defined as the polarity produced in the molecule by the interaction of two $\pi$-bonds or between a $\pi$-bond and lone pair of electrons present on an adjacent atom. Thus, (D) matches with Resonance effect (III).

Therefore, the correct matching is (A)-(IV), (B)-(I), (C)-(II), (D)-(III).

Answer: (A)-(IV), (B)-(I), (C)-(II), (D)-(III)

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: The heterolytic cleavage of the $\text{C}-\text{Br}$ bond in 2-bromo-2-methylbutane yields a carbocation intermediate. What is the number of hyperconjugative structures possible for this resulting carbocation?
questions.solution:
First, deduce the structure of the starting compound. 2-Bromo-2-methylbutane is $\text{CH}_3-\text{C}(\text{Br})(\text{CH}_3)-\text{CH}_2-\text{CH}_3$.

Heterolytic cleavage of the $\text{C}-\text{Br}$ bond results in the formation of the 2-methylbutan-2-yl carbocation: $\text{CH}_3-\text{C}^+(\text{CH}_3)-\text{CH}_2-\text{CH}_3$.

To find the number of hyperconjugative structures, count the number of $\alpha$-hydrogens attached to the carbons directly bonded to the positively charged carbon.

The $\alpha$-carbons are:
- C1 methyl group: 3 $\alpha$-hydrogens
- C2 methyl branch: 3 $\alpha$-hydrogens
- C3 methylene group: 2 $\alpha$-hydrogens

Total $\alpha$-hydrogens = $3 + 3 + 2 = 8$.

Therefore, 8 hyperconjugative structures are possible for this carbocation.

Answer: $8$

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q:
Consider the following statements regarding the stereochemistry of organic compounds:

(I) Propan-2-ol is a chiral molecule.
(II) Butan-2-ol exists as two non-superimposable mirror images.
(III) The $\text{S}_\text{N}1$ hydrolysis of 2-bromo-2-methylbutane yields an optically active mixture.
(IV) 1-chloro-1-fluoroethane is an achiral molecule.

How many of the above statements are correct?
questions.solution:
Let us evaluate each statement:

(I) Incorrect. Propan-2-ol ($\text{CH}_3\text{CH(OH)CH}_3$) has two identical methyl groups attached to the central carbon. Therefore, it lacks a chiral center and is achiral.

(II) Correct. Butan-2-ol ($\text{CH}_3\text{CH(OH)CH}_2\text{CH}_3$) has four different groups attached to the second carbon atom ($\text{-H}$, $\text{-OH}$, $\text{-CH}_3$, $\text{-CH}_2\text{CH}_3$). It is a chiral molecule and exists as a pair of enantiomers (non-superimposable mirror images).

(III) Incorrect. 2-bromo-2-methylbutane ($\text{CH}_3\text{C(Br)(CH}_3\text{)CH}_2\text{CH}_3$) has two identical methyl groups on the second carbon, making it an achiral molecule. Its hydrolysis product, 2-methylbutan-2-ol, is also achiral and optically inactive.

(IV) Incorrect. 1-chloro-1-fluoroethane ($\text{CH}_3\text{CH(Cl)(F)}$) has four different groups attached to the first carbon atom ($\text{-H}$, $\text{-Cl}$, $\text{-F}$, $\text{-CH}_3$). It contains a chiral center and is a chiral molecule.

Thus, only statement (II) is correct.

Answer: One

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q:
Given below are two statements: one is labelled as Assertion (A) and the other is labelled as Reason (R).

Assertion (A): Diphenyl ether is significantly more difficult to protonate than diethyl ether.
Reason (R): The phenyl rings in diphenyl ether decrease the electron density on oxygen primarily through a strong $-I$ (inductive) effect.

In the light of the above statements, choose the most appropriate answer from the options given below:
options: Both (A) and (R) are correct and (R) is the correct explanation of (A)
Both (A) and (R) are correct but (R) is not the correct explanation of (A)
(A) is correct but (R) is not correct
(A) is not correct but (R) is correct
questions.solution:
Assertion (A) is correct because the lone pairs on the oxygen atom in diphenyl ether are delocalized into the two benzene rings, making them less available for protonation compared to the localized lone pairs in diethyl ether.

Reason (R) is incorrect because the primary cause for the decreased electron density on the oxygen atom is resonance (delocalization of lone pairs into the $\pi$ system of the aromatic rings), not the inductive ($-I$) effect.

Answer: (A) is correct but (R) is not correct

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: Which of the following represents the correct decreasing order of basic strength for methyl substituted amines and ammonia in the gas phase?
questions.solution:
In the gas phase, there are no solvent molecules to stabilize the conjugate acid through hydrogen bonding (solvation effect).

The basic strength of amines in the gas phase is determined solely by the electron-donating inductive effect (+I) of the alkyl groups. More alkyl groups increase the electron density on the nitrogen atom, making it a stronger base.

Thus, the basicity strictly follows the order: tertiary > secondary > primary > ammonia. For methylamines, the correct decreasing order is $(\text{CH}_3)_3\text{N} \gt (\text{CH}_3)_2\text{NH} \gt \text{CH}_3\text{NH}_2 \gt \text{NH}_3$.

Answer: $(\text{CH}_3)_3\text{N} \gt (\text{CH}_3)_2\text{NH} \gt \text{CH}_3\text{NH}_2 \gt \text{NH}_3$

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: An unknown alkene 'X' with the molecular formula $\mathrm{C_6H_{12}}$ yields 2-methylpentane upon catalytic hydrogenation. If 'X' exhibits geometrical isomerism, what is the IUPAC name of 'X'?
questions.solution:
Since catalytic hydrogenation of alkene 'X' yields 2-methylpentane, 'X' must possess the same carbon skeleton as 2-methylpentane.

The possible alkenes with this skeleton are:
1. 2-Methylpent-1-ene: $\mathrm{CH_2=C(CH_3)-CH_2-CH_2-CH_3}$
2. 2-Methylpent-2-ene: $\mathrm{(CH_3)_2C=CH-CH_2-CH_3}$
3. 4-Methylpent-2-ene: $\mathrm{CH_3-CH(CH_3)-CH=CH-CH_3}$
4. 4-Methylpent-1-ene: $\mathrm{CH_3-CH(CH_3)-CH_2-CH=CH_2}$

For an alkene to exhibit geometrical isomerism (GI), each carbon atom of the double bond must be bonded to two different atoms or groups.

Evaluating the candidates:
- 2-Methylpent-1-ene and 4-Methylpent-1-ene have terminal $\mathrm{=CH_2}$ groups (two identical hydrogen atoms on one carbon). They do not show GI.
- 2-Methylpent-2-ene has two identical methyl groups attached to one of the double-bonded carbons. It does not show GI.
- 4-Methylpent-2-ene has a hydrogen atom and an isopropyl group on one double-bonded carbon, and a hydrogen atom and a methyl group on the other. It satisfies the condition and exhibits GI.

Therefore, the alkene 'X' is 4-methylpent-2-ene.

Answer: 4-Methylpent-2-ene

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: Which of the following molecular formulas representing amines can exhibit metamerism?
questions.solution:
Metamerism arises due to the unequal distribution of alkyl groups on either side of a polyvalent functional group (such as -O-, -S-, -NH-, -CO-).

For amines to show metamerism, they must be secondary or tertiary amines with enough carbon atoms to form at least two different structural arrangements.

$CH_5N$ can only form methylamine, a primary amine.

$C_2H_7N$ can form dimethylamine ($CH_3-NH-CH_3$), a secondary amine, but only one arrangement is possible.

$C_3H_9N$ can form ethylmethylamine ($CH_3CH_2-NH-CH_3$), but again, only one secondary amine arrangement is possible.

$C_4H_{11}N$ can form diethylamine ($CH_3CH_2-NH-CH_2CH_3$) and methylpropylamine ($CH_3-NH-CH_2CH_2CH_3$). Since the alkyl groups attached to the polyvalent -NH- group are different, these two structures are metamers.

Answer: $C_4H_{11}N$

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: A mixture contains two isomers, $o$-nitrophenol and $p$-nitrophenol. Which of the following represents the most suitable technique for their separation and the correct underlying chemical reason?
options: Fractional distillation; due to a large difference in their molecular weights.
Distillation under reduced pressure; because both isomers decompose at their normal boiling points.
Steam distillation; because $o$-nitrophenol forms intermolecular hydrogen bonds with water making it highly soluble.
Steam distillation; because $o$-nitrophenol is steam volatile due to intramolecular hydrogen bonding while $p$-nitrophenol is not.
questions.solution:
The correct technique to separate a mixture of $o$-nitrophenol and $p$-nitrophenol is steam distillation.

$o$-Nitrophenol exhibits intramolecular hydrogen bonding, which prevents the association of its molecules, making it more volatile (steam volatile).

In contrast, $p$-nitrophenol exhibits intermolecular hydrogen bonding, leading to molecular association and a higher boiling point, making it less volatile.

Because of this significant difference in their steam volatility, steam distillation effectively separates the two isomers.

Answer: Steam distillation; because $o$-nitrophenol is steam volatile due to intramolecular hydrogen bonding while $p$-nitrophenol is not.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: An organic compound containing both nitrogen and sulphur is fused with an insufficient amount of sodium metal. The resulting sodium fusion extract is then treated with $\mathrm{Fe}^{3+}$ ions. Which of the following correctly identifies the primary sodium salt formed during the fusion and the colour observed upon the addition of $\mathrm{Fe}^{3+}$?
questions.solution:
When an organic compound containing both nitrogen and sulphur is fused with an insufficient amount of sodium metal, sodium thiocyanate ($\mathrm{NaSCN}$) is formed instead of separate sodium cyanide and sodium sulphide.

$\mathrm{Na} + \mathrm{C} + \mathrm{N} + \mathrm{S} \rightarrow \mathrm{NaSCN}$

Upon addition of $\mathrm{Fe}^{3+}$ ions to the extract, a blood-red colouration is observed due to the formation of the ferrithiocyanate complex, $[\mathrm{Fe}(\mathrm{SCN})]^{2+}$.

$\mathrm{Fe}^{3+} + \mathrm{SCN}^{-} \rightarrow [\mathrm{Fe}(\mathrm{SCN})]^{2+}$

If excess sodium were used, the thiocyanate would decompose into cyanide and sulphide, yielding the standard independent tests.

Answer: $\mathrm{NaSCN}$, Blood red

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q:
Match List-I with List-II.

List-IList-II
(A) Enantiomers(I) Optically inactive due to internal compensation
(B) Racemic mixture(II) Complete inversion of configuration
(C) Meso compound(III) Non-superimposable mirror images
(D) $\text{S}_{\text{N}}2$ reaction(IV) Optically inactive due to external compensation

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
questions.solution:
Enantiomers (A) are stereoisomers that are non-superimposable mirror images of each other, matching with (III).

A racemic mixture (B) contains equal amounts of two enantiomers, and their optical rotations cancel each other out. Thus, it is optically inactive due to external compensation, matching with (IV).

A meso compound (C) contains chiral centers but has an internal plane of symmetry, making the molecule achiral overall. It is optically inactive due to internal compensation, matching with (I).

An $\text{S}_{\text{N}}2$ reaction (D) proceeds with the nucleophile attacking from the side opposite to the leaving group, leading to complete inversion of configuration, matching with (II).

Therefore, the correct matching sequence is A-III, B-IV, C-I, D-II.

Answer: A-III, B-IV, C-I, D-II

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: Determine the total number of allylic hydrogen atoms present in one molecule of 2,5-Dimethylhex-2-ene.
questions.solution:
First, draw the structure of 2,5-Dimethylhex-2-ene based on its IUPAC name: $CH_3-C(CH_3)=CH-CH_2-CH(CH_3)-CH_3$.

Identify the $sp^2$ hybridized carbon atoms of the double bond, which are C2 and C3.

Allylic carbons are the $sp^3$ hybridized carbon atoms directly attached to the $sp^2$ carbons. In this molecule, the allylic carbons are C1, the methyl group attached to C2, and C4.

Count the hydrogen atoms on these allylic carbons: 3 (from C1) + 3 (from the C2 methyl group) + 2 (from C4) = 8 allylic hydrogens.

Counting only the vinylic hydrogen gives 1, counting only the methyls on C2 gives 6, and counting all hydrogens in the molecule gives 16.

Answer: 8

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q:
Match List I with List II:

List IList II
A. Isopropyl cationI. Highly unstable due to positive charge on sp hybridized carbon
B. Allyl cationII. Stabilized by hyperconjugation involving 6 $\alpha$-hydrogens
C. Benzyl cationIII. Stabilized by resonance with one $\pi$ bond
D. Vinyl cationIV. Stabilized by resonance with a benzene ring

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
questions.solution:
Isopropyl cation $(CH_3)_2CH^+$ has 6 $\alpha$-hydrogens, so it is stabilized by hyperconjugation (A → II).

Allyl cation $CH_2=CH-CH_2^+$ is stabilized by resonance involving one adjacent $\pi$ bond (B → III).

Benzyl cation $C_6H_5CH_2^+$ is stabilized by extensive resonance delocalization with the benzene ring (C → IV).

Vinyl cation $CH_2=CH^+$ has the positive charge on an electronegative sp hybridized carbon, making it highly unstable (D → I).

Therefore, the correct matching is A-II, B-III, C-IV, D-I.

Answer: A-II, B-III, C-IV, D-I

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q:
Match List-I with List-II:

List-I (Pairs of compounds)List-II (Type of isomerism)
(A) Diethylamine and Methyl propylamine(I) Chain isomerism
(B) Butan-1-ol and Butan-2-ol(II) Position isomerism
(C) Pentane and Isopentane(III) Functional isomerism
(D) Propanone and Propanal(IV) Metamerism

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
questions.solution:
(A) Diethylamine ($CH_3CH_2-NH-CH_2CH_3$) and Methyl propylamine ($CH_3-NH-CH_2CH_2CH_3$) have different alkyl groups attached to the polyvalent -NH- group. They exhibit metamerism. (A → IV)

(B) Butan-1-ol and Butan-2-ol differ only in the position of the -OH group on the main carbon chain. They exhibit position isomerism. (B → II)

(C) Pentane (a straight chain) and Isopentane (a branched chain) differ in their carbon skeletons. They exhibit chain isomerism. (C → I)

(D) Propanone is a ketone and Propanal is an aldehyde. Since they have different functional groups but the same molecular formula ($C_3H_6O$), they exhibit functional isomerism. (D → III)

Therefore, the correct matching is (A)-(IV), (B)-(II), (C)-(I), (D)-(III).

Answer: (A)-(IV), (B)-(II), (C)-(I), (D)-(III)

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: Consider the molecule 4-(2-hydroxyethyl)phenol. When this compound is treated with one equivalent of a dilute strong acid, which site is preferentially protonated?
options: The oxygen atom of the phenolic $-OH$ group
The carbon atoms of the benzene ring
The oxygen atom of the aliphatic $-OH$ group
questions.solution:
The molecule 4-(2-hydroxyethyl)phenol contains two types of hydroxyl groups: a phenolic $-OH$ and an aliphatic primary $-OH$.

Protonation requires the availability of a lone pair of electrons on the oxygen atom. In the phenolic $-OH$ group, the lone pairs on oxygen are delocalized into the benzene ring through resonance ($+R$ effect), making them less available to accept a proton.

In the aliphatic $-OH$ group, the lone pairs are localized and their electron density is slightly enhanced by the $+I$ effect of the alkyl chain. Therefore, the aliphatic $-OH$ group is significantly more basic and will be preferentially protonated.

Answer: The oxygen atom of the aliphatic $-OH$ group

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q:
Given below are two statements: one is labelled as Assertion (A) and the other is labelled as Reason (R).

Assertion (A): The IUPAC name of the compound $\text{CH}_3-\text{C}(\text{CH}_3)_2-\text{CH}_2-\text{CH}=\text{CH}-\text{CH}_3$ is 5,5-Dimethylhex-2-ene.
Reason (R): In the IUPAC nomenclature of alkenes, the parent chain must contain the maximum number of carbon atoms including the double bond.

In the light of the above statements, choose the most appropriate answer from the options given below:
options: Both (A) and (R) are correct and (R) is the correct explanation of (A)
Both (A) and (R) are correct but (R) is not the correct explanation of (A)
(A) is correct but (R) is not correct
(A) is not correct but (R) is correct
questions.solution:
Assertion (A) is correct. The longest carbon chain containing the double bond has 6 carbon atoms. Numbering is done from the right side to give the lowest possible locant to the principal functional group (the double bond), which gets position 2. If numbered from the left, the double bond would be at position 4. Thus, the correct IUPAC name is 5,5-Dimethylhex-2-ene.

Reason (R) is also correct as a general rule of IUPAC nomenclature, but it does not explain the specific numbering direction chosen in the Assertion. The correct explanation for the Assertion is the lowest locant rule for the principal functional group.

Therefore, both (A) and (R) are correct but (R) is not the correct explanation of (A).

Answer: Both (A) and (R) are correct but (R) is not the correct explanation of (A)

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: What is the correct IUPAC name of the compound $CH_3-CH=C(OH)-C \equiv CH$, and what is the hybridization state of the carbon atom bearing the hydroxyl group?
questions.solution:
Identify the principal functional group, which is the -OH group. The longest carbon chain containing the -OH group and the multiple bonds has 5 carbon atoms (root word: pent).

Number the chain to give the principal functional group the lowest possible locant. Numbering from either left to right or right to left gives the -OH group position 3.

Apply the lowest locant rule for the multiple bonds. Numbering from right to left gives multiple bonds positions 1 and 3. Numbering from left to right gives positions 2 and 4. The locant set (1, 3) is lower than (2, 4), so we must number from right to left.

The suffixes for multiple bonds are arranged alphabetically. 'en' comes before 'yn'. The correct IUPAC name is pent-3-en-1-yn-3-ol.

The carbon atom at position 3 is bonded to one -OH group (single bond), one carbon atom via a single bond, and one carbon atom via a double bond. It forms 3 sigma bonds and 1 pi bond, so its hybridization state is $sp^2$.

Answer: pent-3-en-1-yn-3-ol ; $sp^2$

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q:
Given below are two statements: one is labelled as Assertion (A) and the other is labelled as Reason (R).

Assertion (A): In Lassaigne's test, an organic compound containing both nitrogen and sulphur gives a Prussian blue colour with $\text{Fe}^{3+}$ ions.

Reason (R): During sodium fusion of such compounds, sodium thiocyanate is formed, which provides $\text{SCN}^{-}$ ions to form the blood-red $[\text{Fe}(\text{SCN})]^{2+}$ complex.

In the light of the above statements, choose the most appropriate answer from the options given below:
options: Both Assertion and Reason are true and Reason is the correct explanation of Assertion.
Both Assertion and Reason are true but Reason is not the correct explanation of Assertion.
Assertion is true but Reason is false.
Assertion is false but Reason is true.
questions.solution:
Assertion (A) is false because in Lassaigne's test, an organic compound containing both nitrogen and sulphur forms sodium thiocyanate ($\text{NaSCN}$) during fusion. This extract gives a blood-red colour with $\text{Fe}^{3+}$ ions, not a Prussian blue colour. Prussian blue is observed when only nitrogen is present.

Reason (R) is true as the fusion of an organic compound containing both N and S with sodium yields $\text{NaSCN}$. The $\text{SCN}^{-}$ ions react with $\text{Fe}^{3+}$ to form the blood-red thiocyanatoiron(III) complex, $[\text{Fe}(\text{SCN})]^{2+}$.

Answer: Assertion is false but Reason is true.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q:
Three different liquid mixtures are described below based on their physical properties:
Mixture X: Contains two miscible liquids with a boiling point difference of $8\text{ K}$.
Mixture Y: Contains an organic liquid which is immiscible with water but volatile in steam.
Mixture Z: Contains a liquid that has a normal boiling point of $550\text{ K}$ but decomposes at $480\text{ K}$.

Which of the following represents the most suitable sequence of purification techniques for Mixture X, Mixture Y, and Mixture Z respectively?
options: Fractional distillation, Steam distillation, Distillation under reduced pressure
Simple distillation, Steam distillation, Distillation under reduced pressure
Fractional distillation, Solvent extraction, Distillation under reduced pressure
Fractional distillation, Steam distillation, Simple distillation
questions.solution:
Mixture X contains liquids with a small boiling point difference ($8\text{ K}$). Such mixtures cannot be separated by simple distillation and require fractional distillation.

Mixture Y contains an organic liquid that is immiscible with water and volatile in steam. The standard technique for purifying such substances is steam distillation.

Mixture Z contains a high-boiling liquid that decomposes below its normal boiling point. It must be purified using distillation under reduced pressure (vacuum distillation), which lowers the boiling point and prevents decomposition.

Therefore, the correct sequence is Fractional distillation, Steam distillation, and Distillation under reduced pressure.

Answer: Fractional distillation, Steam distillation, Distillation under reduced pressure

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q:
Given below are two statements: one is labelled as Assertion (A) and the other is labelled as Reason (R).

Assertion (A): Toluene undergoes electrophilic aromatic substitution faster than benzene.

Reason (R): The methyl group in toluene increases the electron density in the benzene ring predominantly through its +I (inductive) effect, which outweighs the hyperconjugation effect.

In the light of the above statements, choose the most appropriate answer from the options given below:
options: Both Assertion (A) and Reason (R) are true and Reason (R) is the correct explanation of Assertion (A).
Both Assertion (A) and Reason (R) are true but Reason (R) is not the correct explanation of Assertion (A).
Assertion (A) is true but Reason (R) is false.
Assertion (A) is false but Reason (R) is true.
questions.solution:
Assertion (A) is true: Toluene has a methyl group attached to the benzene ring, which acts as an electron-donating group. This increases the electron density on the ring, making it more reactive towards electrophilic aromatic substitution than benzene.

Reason (R) is false: The methyl group exerts both a +I (inductive) effect and a hyperconjugation effect. However, hyperconjugation (a permanent delocalisation of $\sigma$-electrons into the $\pi$-system) is a stronger effect than the inductive effect and is predominantly responsible for the increased electron density at the ortho and para positions of the ring.

Therefore, Assertion (A) is true but Reason (R) is false.

Answer: Assertion (A) is true but Reason (R) is false.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q:
Given below are two statements: one is labelled as Assertion (A) and the other is labelled as Reason (R).

Assertion (A): Halogens present in an organic compound cannot be detected by directly adding aqueous silver nitrate solution to the compound.
Reason (R): The elements in organic compounds are covalently bonded and do not furnish free ions in aqueous solution.

In the light of the above statements, choose the most appropriate answer from the options given below:
options: Both (A) and (R) are true but (R) is not the correct explanation of (A)
Both (A) and (R) are true and (R) is the correct explanation of (A)
questions.solution:
Organic compounds generally contain elements like halogens in covalently bonded states. Because they are covalent, they do not ionise in aqueous solutions to furnish free halide ions ($\text{X}^-$).

Aqueous silver nitrate ($\text{AgNO}_3$) reacts only with free halide ions to form a precipitate of silver halide ($\text{AgX}$). Since direct addition of $\text{AgNO}_3$ to the organic compound does not provide free halide ions, no precipitate is formed, and the halogens cannot be detected directly.

Therefore, both Assertion (A) and Reason (R) are true, and (R) is the correct explanation of (A).

Answer: Both (A) and (R) are true and (R) is the correct explanation of (A)

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q:
Consider the following compounds:
I. Cyclohexanol
II. Phenol
III. $p$-Nitrophenol
IV. $p$-Methoxyphenol

The correct decreasing order of their ease of protonation is:
questions.solution:
The ease of protonation (basicity) depends on the availability of the lone pair of electrons on the oxygen atom.

In cyclohexanol (I), the oxygen atom is attached to an $sp^3$ hybridized carbon, and its lone pairs are fully localized. This makes it the most electron-rich and easiest to protonate among the given compounds.

In phenol (II), $p$-nitrophenol (III), and $p$-methoxyphenol (IV), the oxygen atom is attached to an aromatic ring, and its lone pair is delocalized into the ring via resonance, making them less basic than cyclohexanol.

Among the aromatic compounds, substituents affect the electron density on oxygen. The methoxy group in $p$-methoxyphenol (IV) exerts an electron-donating resonance effect (+R), which increases the electron density on the oxygen atom compared to phenol (II).

Conversely, the nitro group in $p$-nitrophenol (III) exerts strong electron-withdrawing resonance and inductive effects (-R, -I), significantly decreasing the electron density on the oxygen atom and making it the most difficult to protonate.

Therefore, the correct decreasing order of ease of protonation is I > IV > II > III. Note that the reverse order (III > II > IV > I) represents their acidic strength.

Answer: I > IV > II > III

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q:
Match List-I with List-II:

List-I (Molecule)List-II (IUPAC Name)
(A) $\text{CH}_2=\text{CH}-\text{C}\equiv\text{CH}$(I) Pent-1-en-4-yne
(B) $\text{CH}_2=\text{CH}-\text{CH}_2-\text{C}\equiv\text{CH}$(II) 2-Methylbuta-1,3-diene
(C) $\text{CH}_3-\text{CH}=\text{CH}-\text{C}\equiv\text{CH}$(III) But-1-en-3-yne
(D) $\text{CH}_2=\text{C}(\text{CH}_3)-\text{CH}=\text{CH}_2$(IV) Pent-3-en-1-yne

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
questions.solution:
According to IUPAC nomenclature rules for compounds containing both double and triple bonds:
1. The parent chain is numbered to give the lowest locant set to the multiple bonds.
2. If there is a choice (tie), the double bond is given the lower number.

For (A) $\text{CH}_2=\text{CH}-\text{C}\equiv\text{CH}$: Numbering from left gives locants 1,3. Numbering from right gives 1,3. Due to the tie, the double bond gets priority. Name: But-1-en-3-yne.

For (B) $\text{CH}_2=\text{CH}-\text{CH}_2-\text{C}\equiv\text{CH}$: Numbering from left gives 1,4. Numbering from right gives 1,4. Tie-breaker gives double bond priority. Name: Pent-1-en-4-yne.

For (C) $\text{CH}_3-\text{CH}=\text{CH}-\text{C}\equiv\text{CH}$: Numbering from right gives locants 1,3. Numbering from left gives 2,4. The lowest locant set is 1,3. Name: Pent-3-en-1-yne.

For (D) $\text{CH}_2=\text{C}(\text{CH}_3)-\text{CH}=\text{CH}_2$: Numbering from left gives the methyl group the lower locant 2. Name: 2-Methylbuta-1,3-diene.

Therefore, the correct matching is (A)-(III), (B)-(I), (C)-(IV), (D)-(II).

Answer: (A)-(III), (B)-(I), (C)-(IV), (D)-(II)

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q:
Consider the following carbocations:
I. 2-Methylbutan-2-yl cation
II. 4-Chloro-2-methylbutan-2-yl cation
III. 2-Methylpropan-2-yl cation

The correct decreasing order of their stability is:
questions.solution:
The stability of alkyl carbocations is determined by the number of $\alpha$-hydrogens (hyperconjugation) and inductive effects.

III. 2-Methylpropan-2-yl cation (tert-butyl cation) has 3 methyl groups attached to the positively charged carbon, giving $3 + 3 + 3 = 9\alpha$-hydrogens.

I. 2-Methylbutan-2-yl cation has two methyl groups and one ethyl group attached to the positively charged carbon, giving $3 + 3 + 2 = 8\alpha$-hydrogens.

II. 4-Chloro-2-methylbutan-2-yl cation also has $3 + 3 + 2 = 8\alpha$-hydrogens. However, the presence of the electronegative chlorine atom exerts a $-I$ (electron-withdrawing inductive) effect, which decreases the electron density on the positively charged carbon, making it less stable than I.

Therefore, the correct decreasing order of stability is III > I > II.

Answer: III > I > II

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q:
Given below are two statements: one is labelled as Assertion (A) and the other is labelled as Reason (R).

Assertion (A): Methyl butanoate and propyl ethanoate are metamers of each other.
Reason (R): Metamerism is exhibited only by organic compounds containing divalent oxygen atoms.

In the light of the above statements, choose the most appropriate answer from the options given below:
options: Both Assertion and Reason are correct and Reason is the correct explanation for Assertion.
Both Assertion and Reason are correct but Reason is not the correct explanation for Assertion.
Assertion is correct but Reason is incorrect.
Assertion is incorrect but Reason is correct.
questions.solution:
Assertion (A) is correct: Methyl butanoate ($\text{CH}_3\text{CH}_2\text{CH}_2-\text{COO}-\text{CH}_3$) and propyl ethanoate ($\text{CH}_3-\text{COO}-\text{CH}_2\text{CH}_2\text{CH}_3$) have the same molecular formula ($\text{C}_5\text{H}_{10}\text{O}_2$) but differ in the alkyl groups attached on either side of the polyvalent ester ($-\text{COO}-$) group. Therefore, they are metamers.

Reason (R) is incorrect: Metamerism is not restricted to compounds with divalent oxygen atoms (like ethers). It is exhibited by any polyvalent functional group, which includes ketones ($-\text{CO}-$), secondary amines ($-\text{NH}-$), and thioethers ($-\text{S}-$).

Answer: Assertion is correct but Reason is incorrect.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q:
During the qualitative analysis of an organic compound, a student adds freshly prepared $\text{FeSO}_{4}$ solution to the Lassaigne's extract, heats the mixture, and then acidifies it with concentrated $\text{H}_{2}\text{SO}_{4}$. A complex with the formula $\text{Fe}_{4}[\text{Fe}(\text{CN})_{6}]_{3}\cdot x\text{H}_{2}\text{O}$ is formed.

What is the characteristic colour of this complex and which element's presence in the organic compound does it confirm?
questions.solution:
The given complex is $\text{Fe}_{4}[\text{Fe}(\text{CN})_{6}]_{3}\cdot x\text{H}_{2}\text{O}$, which is iron(III) hexacyanoferrate(II).

This complex has a characteristic Prussian blue colour.

It is formed during Lassaigne's test when the organic compound contains nitrogen. The nitrogen and carbon from the organic compound fuse with sodium to form sodium cyanide ($\text{NaCN}$).

Upon treatment with $\text{FeSO}_{4}$ and concentrated $\text{H}_{2}\text{SO}_{4}$, the cyanide ions form the Prussian blue complex, confirming the presence of nitrogen.

Answer: Prussian blue, Nitrogen

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q:
Given below are two statements: one is labelled as Assertion (A) and the other is labelled as Reason (R).

Assertion (A): The carbocation $\left(\mathrm{CH}_3\right)_3\mathrm{C}-\stackrel{\oplus}{\mathrm{C}}\mathrm{H}-\mathrm{CH}_3$ is less stable than $\mathrm{CH}_3-\stackrel{\oplus}{\mathrm{C}}\mathrm{H}-\mathrm{CH}_2-\mathrm{CH}_3$.

Reason (R): The $+I$ effect of a tert-butyl group is greater than that of an ethyl group.

In the light of the above statements, choose the most appropriate answer from the options given below:
options: Both Assertion (A) and Reason (R) are true and Reason (R) is the correct explanation of Assertion (A).
Both Assertion (A) and Reason (R) are true but Reason (R) is not the correct explanation of Assertion (A).
Assertion (A) is true but Reason (R) is false.
Assertion (A) is false but Reason (R) is true.
questions.solution:
Assertion (A) is true because the stability of alkyl carbocations is primarily determined by hyperconjugation, which depends on the number of $\alpha$-hydrogen atoms. The carbocation $\left(\mathrm{CH}_3\right)_3\mathrm{C}-\stackrel{\oplus}{\mathrm{C}}\mathrm{H}-\mathrm{CH}_3$ has only 3 $\alpha$-hydrogens (from the right methyl group; the tert-butyl group has no $\alpha$-hydrogens). The carbocation $\mathrm{CH}_3-\stackrel{\oplus}{\mathrm{C}}\mathrm{H}-\mathrm{CH}_2-\mathrm{CH}_3$ has 5 $\alpha$-hydrogens (3 from the left methyl group and 2 from the right methylene group). More $\alpha$-hydrogens result in more hyperconjugative structures, making the latter more stable.

Reason (R) is true because a tert-butyl group has three electron-donating methyl groups, making its $+I$ effect stronger than that of an ethyl group.

However, Reason (R) is not the correct explanation of Assertion (A). If the $+I$ effect were the dominant factor, the first carbocation would be more stable. The actual reason for the higher stability of the second carbocation is the dominance of hyperconjugation over the inductive effect.

Answer: Both Assertion (A) and Reason (R) are true but Reason (R) is not the correct explanation of Assertion (A).

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: What is the minimum number of carbon atoms required for an aliphatic, non-cyclic ketone to exhibit metamerism?
questions.solution:
Metamerism arises due to different alkyl chains on either side of a polyvalent functional group. For ketones, the functional group is the carbonyl group ($-\text{CO}-$), which is divalent.

Let us check the homologous series of aliphatic ketones:
With 3 carbon atoms: $\text{CH}_3-\text{CO}-\text{CH}_3$ (Propanone). No other arrangement of alkyl groups around the carbonyl carbon is possible.
With 4 carbon atoms: $\text{CH}_3-\text{CO}-\text{CH}_2\text{CH}_3$ (Butan-2-one). No other arrangement is possible.
With 5 carbon atoms: The alkyl groups can be a methyl and a propyl group, giving $\text{CH}_3-\text{CO}-\text{CH}_2\text{CH}_2\text{CH}_3$ (Pentan-2-one), or two ethyl groups, giving $\text{CH}_3\text{CH}_2-\text{CO}-\text{CH}_2\text{CH}_3$ (Pentan-3-one). These two compounds are metamers.

Thus, a minimum of 5 carbon atoms is required for an aliphatic ketone to exhibit metamerism.

Answer: 5

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q:
Given below are two statements: one is labelled as Assertion (A) and the other is labelled as Reason (R).

Assertion (A): Isopropyl carbocation is more stable than tert-butyl carbocation.
Reason (R): tert-Butyl carbocation is stabilized by 9 hyperconjugative structures whereas isopropyl carbocation is stabilized by 6 hyperconjugative structures.

In the light of the above statements, choose the most appropriate answer from the options given below.
options: Both (A) and (R) are correct and (R) is the correct explanation of (A)
Both (A) and (R) are correct but (R) is not the correct explanation of (A)
(A) is correct but (R) is not correct
(A) is not correct but (R) is correct
questions.solution:
Assertion (A) is incorrect because tert-butyl carbocation is a $3^{\circ}$ carbocation and is more stable than isopropyl carbocation, which is a $2^{\circ}$ carbocation.

Reason (R) is correct. The stability of alkyl carbocations is governed by hyperconjugation. The tert-butyl carbocation, $(CH_3)_3C^+$, has 9 $\alpha$-hydrogens, leading to 9 hyperconjugative structures. The isopropyl carbocation, $(CH_3)_2CH^+$, has 6 $\alpha$-hydrogens, leading to 6 hyperconjugative structures. Greater the number of hyperconjugative structures, higher is the stability.

Answer: (A) is not correct but (R) is correct

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: Among the following nitrogenous compounds, which one is the most difficult to protonate?
questions.solution:
The ease of protonation of a compound depends on the availability of the lone pair of electrons on the basic atom (nitrogen, in this case).

In methylamine and dimethylamine, the alkyl (methyl) groups exert an electron-donating inductive effect (+I effect), which increases the electron density on the nitrogen atom. This makes their lone pairs more available for protonation compared to ammonia.

In aniline, the nitrogen atom is directly attached to a benzene ring. The lone pair of electrons on the nitrogen atom is delocalized into the aromatic ring through resonance. This delocalization significantly decreases the electron density on the nitrogen atom, making the lone pair least available for protonation.

Therefore, aniline is the most difficult to protonate among the given options.

Answer: Aniline

Assertion (A): Propan-1-ol and Propan-2-ol are considered metamers of each other.
Reason (R): Metamerism arises due to different alkyl chains on either side of the polyvalent functional group.

In the light of the above statements, choose the most appropriate answer from the options given below:
options: Both (A) and (R) are correct and (R) is the correct explanation of (A)
Both (A) and (R) are correct but (R) is not the correct explanation of (A)
(A) is correct but (R) is not correct
(A) is not correct but (R) is correct
questions.solution:
Assertion (A) is not correct because Propan-1-ol ($\text{CH}_3\text{CH}_2\text{CH}_2\text{OH}$) and Propan-2-ol ($\text{CH}_3\text{CH(OH)CH}_3$) differ only in the position of the $-\text{OH}$ group on the carbon chain. They are position isomers, not metamers. Furthermore, the hydroxyl group ($-\text{OH}$) is a monovalent functional group and cannot exhibit metamerism.

Reason (R) is correct as it states the exact definition of metamerism according to NCERT. Metamerism occurs when isomers have the same molecular formula but differ in the nature of the alkyl groups attached to the same polyvalent functional group (such as $-\text{O}-$, $-\text{S}-$, or $-\text{CO}-$).

Therefore, (A) is not correct but (R) is correct.

Answer: (A) is not correct but (R) is correct

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q:
Given below are two statements: one is labelled as Assertion (A) and the other is labelled as Reason (R).

Assertion (A): In aqueous solution, dimethylamine is a stronger base than trimethylamine.
Reason (R): Steric hindrance and lesser hydration of the conjugate acid of trimethylamine decrease its basic strength compared to dimethylamine.

In the light of the above statements, choose the most appropriate answer from the options given below:
options: Both (A) and (R) are correct and (R) is the correct explanation of (A).
Both (A) and (R) are correct but (R) is not the correct explanation of (A).
(A) is correct but (R) is not correct.
(A) is not correct but (R) is correct.
questions.solution:
Assertion (A) is correct. In aqueous solution, the order of basic strength for methyl-substituted amines is secondary > primary > tertiary. Thus, dimethylamine is a stronger base than trimethylamine.

Reason (R) is also correct and explains the assertion. While the $+\text{I}$ effect of three methyl groups in trimethylamine increases electron density on nitrogen, the bulky methyl groups cause steric hindrance to protonation. Furthermore, the conjugate acid of trimethylamine has only one hydrogen atom available for hydrogen bonding with water, leading to lesser hydration (solvation) compared to the conjugate acid of dimethylamine. This combination of steric hindrance and reduced solvation makes trimethylamine a weaker base than dimethylamine in aqueous solution.

Answer: Both (A) and (R) are correct and (R) is the correct explanation of (A).

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q:
Given below are two statements: one is labelled as Assertion (A) and the other is labelled as Reason (R).

Assertion (A): 1,2-Dimethylcyclobutane exhibits geometrical isomerism whereas 1,1-dimethylcyclobutane does not.
Reason (R): For geometrical isomerism in cycloalkanes, at least two ring carbons must be $\mathrm{sp}^3$ hybridized and each must be bonded to two different atoms or groups.

In the light of the above statements, choose the most appropriate answer from the options given below:
options: Both Assertion (A) and Reason (R) are true and Reason (R) is the correct explanation of Assertion (A).
Both Assertion (A) and Reason (R) are true but Reason (R) is not the correct explanation of Assertion (A).
Assertion (A) is true but Reason (R) is false.
Assertion (A) is false but Reason (R) is true.
questions.solution:
Assertion (A) is true: 1,2-Dimethylcyclobutane has two adjacent $\mathrm{sp}^3$ hybridized carbons (C-1 and C-2), each bonded to a hydrogen atom and a methyl group. Because these two carbons each have two different groups, the molecule can exist as cis and trans isomers. In contrast, 1,1-dimethylcyclobutane has two identical methyl groups on the same carbon (C-1), so it cannot show geometrical isomerism.

Reason (R) is true: The necessary condition for geometrical isomerism in cycloalkanes is that at least two $\mathrm{sp}^3$ hybridized ring carbons must each be bonded to two different atoms or groups.

Reason (R) correctly explains why 1,2-dimethylcyclobutane shows geometrical isomerism while 1,1-dimethylcyclobutane does not. Therefore, both Assertion (A) and Reason (R) are true and Reason (R) is the correct explanation of Assertion (A).

Answer: Both Assertion (A) and Reason (R) are true and Reason (R) is the correct explanation of Assertion (A).

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: The correct decreasing order of the basic strength of ethyl substituted amines and ammonia in aqueous solution is:
questions.solution:
In aqueous solution, the basic strength of amines depends on the combined effect of the inductive effect (+I), solvation (hydrogen bonding with water), and steric hindrance.

For ethyl substituted amines, the larger size of the ethyl group compared to the methyl group causes steric hindrance to play a more significant role, altering the balance between solvation and the +I effect.

The resulting order of basicity for ethylamines in aqueous solution is secondary > tertiary > primary > ammonia. Therefore, the correct decreasing order is $(\text{C}_2\text{H}_5)_2\text{NH} \gt (\text{C}_2\text{H}_5)_3\text{N} \gt \text{C}_2\text{H}_5\text{NH}_2 \gt \text{NH}_3$.

Answer: $(\text{C}_2\text{H}_5)_2\text{NH} \gt (\text{C}_2\text{H}_5)_3\text{N} \gt \text{C}_2\text{H}_5\text{NH}_2 \gt \text{NH}_3$

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q:
Given below are four statements regarding the purification of organic compounds:

Statement I: Simple distillation is used to separate liquids having a boiling point difference of less than 10 K.
Statement II: In fractional distillation, the fractionating column provides surfaces for heat exchange between ascending vapours and descending condensed liquid.
Statement III: Glycerol is separated from spent-lye using distillation under reduced pressure because it decomposes at its normal boiling point.
Statement IV: Steam distillation is applied to separate organic liquids that are completely miscible with water and are steam volatile.

How many of the given statements are correct?
questions.solution:
Statement I is incorrect because simple distillation is used for liquids with a sufficient difference in boiling points. For liquids with a small boiling point difference (such as less than 10 K), fractional distillation is required.

Statement II is correct as the fractionating column provides a large surface area for heat exchange between the ascending vapours and the descending condensed liquid.

Statement III is correct because glycerol decomposes at its normal boiling point, so it must be distilled under reduced pressure (vacuum distillation) to lower its boiling temperature.

Statement IV is incorrect because steam distillation is applied to separate substances which are steam volatile but are immiscible with water, not miscible.

Therefore, exactly two statements (II and III) are correct.

Answer: Only two

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q:
Given below are two statements: one is labelled as Assertion (A) and the other is labelled as Reason (R).

Assertion (A): In steam distillation, the organic liquid vaporises at a temperature lower than its normal boiling point.
Reason (R): The organic liquid boils when the sum of its vapour pressure and the vapour pressure of water equals the atmospheric pressure.

In the light of the above statements, choose the most appropriate answer from the options given below:
options: Both Assertion and Reason are correct but Reason is not the correct explanation for Assertion
Both Assertion and Reason are correct and Reason is the correct explanation for Assertion
Assertion is correct but Reason is incorrect
Assertion is incorrect but Reason is correct
questions.solution:
Assertion (A) is correct. In steam distillation, the organic liquid vaporises at a lower temperature than its normal boiling point, which prevents its decomposition.

Reason (R) is also correct and explains Assertion (A). During steam distillation, the mixture of the immiscible organic liquid and water boils when the sum of their vapour pressures equals the atmospheric pressure ($P_{\text{total}} = p_{\text{organic}} + p_{\text{water}} = P_{\text{atm}}$).

Because the partial vapour pressure of the organic liquid ($p_{\text{organic}}$) is less than the atmospheric pressure ($P_{\text{atm}}$), it reaches this required vapour pressure at a temperature lower than its normal boiling point. Thus, Reason (R) is the correct explanation for Assertion (A).

Answer: Both Assertion and Reason are correct and Reason is the correct explanation for Assertion

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: 2-Butene is thermodynamically more stable than 1-butene. Which of the following primary electronic displacement effects is responsible for this difference in stability?
questions.solution:
The stability of alkenes is primarily determined by the number of $\alpha$-hydrogens attached to the $sp^2$ hybridized carbon atoms, which participate in hyperconjugation.

2-Butene ($\text{CH}_3-\text{CH}=\text{CH}-\text{CH}_3$) has 6 $\alpha$-hydrogens, leading to more extensive hyperconjugation.

1-Butene ($\text{CH}_2=\text{CH}-\text{CH}_2-\text{CH}_3$) has only 2 $\alpha$-hydrogens.

The greater the number of hyperconjugative structures, the more stable the alkene. While the $+I$ effect is present, hyperconjugation is the dominating factor for alkene stability. The electromeric effect is a temporary effect requiring an attacking reagent, and the resonance effect requires an extended conjugated $\pi$ system which is absent in these simple alkenes.

Answer: Hyperconjugation

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: Among the following substituted cyclohexyl carbocations, which one is stabilized by the maximum number of hyperconjugative structures?
questions.solution:
The number of hyperconjugative structures for a carbocation is equal to the number of $\alpha$-hydrogens attached to the positively charged carbon.

For the 1-methylcyclohexyl cation, the positively charged carbon is attached to a methyl group (which provides 3 $\alpha$-hydrogens) and two adjacent ring carbons (which provide 2 $\alpha$-hydrogens each). Total $\alpha$-hydrogens = $3 + 2 + 2 = 7$.

For the 1-ethylcyclohexyl cation, the ethyl group provides 2 $\alpha$-hydrogens. Total $\alpha$-hydrogens = $2 + 4 = 6$.

For the 1-isopropylcyclohexyl cation, the isopropyl group provides 1 $\alpha$-hydrogen. Total $\alpha$-hydrogens = $1 + 4 = 5$.

For the 1-tert-butylcyclohexyl cation, the tert-butyl group provides 0 $\alpha$-hydrogens. Total $\alpha$-hydrogens = $0 + 4 = 4$.

Therefore, the 1-methylcyclohexyl cation has the maximum number of $\alpha$-hydrogens and is stabilized by the maximum number of hyperconjugative structures.

Answer: 1-Methylcyclohexyl cation

questions.solution:
The dispersal of the charge stabilizes the carbocation. More the number of electron donating groups are present, greater the dispersal of positive charge and therefore more the stability of carbocation can be observed.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q:
How many geometrical isomers are possible in the following two alkenes ?
(i) $\mathrm{CH}_3-\mathrm{CH}=\mathrm{CH}-\mathrm{CH}=\mathrm{CH}-\mathrm{CH}_3$
(ii) $\mathrm{CH}_3-\mathrm{CH}=\mathrm{CH}-\mathrm{CH}=\mathrm{CH}-\mathrm{Cl}$
questions.solution:
When the ends of alkene containing $n$ double bonds are different, the number of geometrical isomers is $2^n$. Thus for
$\mathrm{CH}_3-\mathrm{CH}=\mathrm{CH}-\mathrm{CH}=\mathrm{CH}-\mathrm{Cl}$.
Number of geometrical isomers $=2^2=4$ When the ends of alkene containing $n$ double bonds are same, then the number of geometrical isomers $=2^{n-1}+2^{p-1}$
where $p=\frac{n}{2}$ for even $n$ and $\frac{n+1}{2}$ for odd $n$, thus for
$\mathrm{CH}_3-\mathrm{CH}=\mathrm{CH}-\mathrm{CH}=\mathrm{CH}-\mathrm{CH}_3$
Number of geometrical isomers
$=2^{2-1}+2^{\frac{2}{2}-1}=2^1+2^0=2+1=3$.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: Which amongst the following is the most stable carbocation?
questions.solution:
The most stable carbocation is $t$-alkyl carbocation because the order of stability of alkyl carbocation is $t$-alkyl $\gt s$-alkyl > p-alkyl $\gt\mathrm{CH}_3^{+}$ carbocation. This stability order is described with the help of hyperconjugation and inductive effect. On the basis of hyper conjugation, $\left(\mathrm{CH}_3\right)_2 \stackrel{+}{\mathrm{C}} \mathrm{H}$ shows six resonating structures due to presence of six $\alpha \mathrm{C}-\mathrm{H}$ bonds,

due to presence of nine $\alpha \mathrm{C}-\mathrm{H}$ bonds $\stackrel{+}{\mathrm{C}} \mathrm{H}_3$ does not show the property of resonance while $\mathrm{CH}_3-\stackrel{+}{\mathrm{C}} \mathrm{H}_2$ shows three resonating structures due to presence of three $\alpha\mathrm{C}-\mathrm{H}$ bonds. Hence, larger number of resonating structures are possible in (2), so it is most stable. The above order of stability is also explained with the help of (+) I-effect of $-\mathrm{CH}_3$ group. More the number of $-\mathrm{CH}_3$ group. more will be tendency to displace the electrons towards positive charged carbon of carbocation. Thus (+) charge is decreased or compensated i.e, positive charge is decreased and stability of carbocation is increased.
